# Papal inauguration of Pope Leo XIV

The **papal inauguration of Pope Leo XIV** was the liturgical service celebrated on May 18, 2025, to formally mark the beginning of the Petrine ministry of the 267th pope of the Catholic Church. Pope Leo XIV, formerly Cardinal Robert Francis Prevost, was elected on May 8, 2025, following the death of Pope Francis in April 2025. The inauguration took place in St. Peter's Square in Vatican City.

The event, officially known as the Mass for the Beginning of the Petrine Ministry of the Bishop of Rome, was attended by an estimated 150,000 to 200,000 people, including official delegations from approximately 150 countries and various religious leaders , , . During the ceremony, the new pope received the papal pallium and the Ring of the Fisherman, the primary symbols of papal authority , . Leo XIV is the first pope from the United States and the first from the Order of Saint Augustine , .

## Background

Pope Francis died on April 21, 2025, at the age of 88, following a period of hospitalization for respiratory issues , . The subsequent papal conclave began on May 7, 2025, with 133 cardinal electors present in the Sistine Chapel , .

On May 8, 2025, on the fourth ballot, the College of Cardinals elected Robert Francis Prevost, an Augustinian friar and the Prefect of the Dicastery for Bishops, as the new Supreme Pontiff , . He took the papal name Leo XIV, a choice that observers noted paid homage to Pope Leo XIII and his focus on social teaching, while also sharing a name with a fictional pope from the 1986 film *Saving Grace* , .

Following his election, the new pope celebrated his first Mass with the cardinals in the Sistine Chapel on May 9 and delivered his first *Urbi et Orbi* blessing , . The inauguration Mass was scheduled for May 18, the Fifth Sunday of Easter , .

## Inauguration Mass

The Mass began at 10:00 a.m. Central European Summer Time (CEST) , . The liturgy followed the "Order of Rites of the Beginning of the Petrine Ministry as Bishop of Rome," a liturgical book approved by Pope Benedict XVI in 2005 and revised in 2013 .

### Procession and Rites at the Tomb
Before the Mass, Pope Leo XIV descended to the tomb of Saint Peter inside St. Peter's Basilica to pray. He was accompanied by the patriarchs and major archbishops of the Eastern Catholic Churches , . During this time, the pallium and the Ring of the Fisherman were placed by the tomb .

The pope then processed from the basilica into St. Peter's Square while the *Laudes Regiae* (Royal Praises) were chanted, invoking the intercession of saints for the new pontiff , .

### Imposition of the Pallium and Ring
The rites specific to the inauguration occurred before the Liturgy of the Word.
* **The Pallium:** Cardinal Mario Zenari, the Apostolic Nuncio to Syria, representing the order of Cardinal Deacons, placed the papal pallium on Pope Leo XIV's shoulders , . The pallium used was the same style as that worn by metropolitan archbishops, distinct from the modified versions used early in the pontificates of Benedict XVI and Francis .
* **The Ring of the Fisherman:** Cardinal Luis Antonio Tagle, representing the order of Cardinal Bishops, presented the Ring of the Fisherman to the pope . The ring is made of gold-plated silver and depicts Saint Peter with the keys, along with the pope's regnal name , .
* **Prayer and Obedience:** Cardinal Fridolin Ambongo Besungu of Kinshasa, representing the Cardinal Priests, led the prayer for the new pope , . Subsequently, twelve representatives of the Catholic Church—including clergy, religious, and laity—approached the pope to profess their obedience , .

### Liturgy
The Gospel was proclaimed in both Greek and Latin to signify the unity of the Eastern and Western Churches , . Pope Leo XIV used the pastoral staff (ferula) previously used by Pope Paul VI and Pope John Paul II , .

## Homily

Pope Leo XIV delivered a homily focused on the themes of unity, reconciliation, and service. He began by quoting Saint Augustine, the founder of his religious order: "Lord, you have made us for yourself, and our heart is restless until it rests in you" , .

The pope described the mission of the papacy through the dimensions of "love and unity" , . He stated:
> "I would like that our first great desire be for a united Church, a sign of unity and communion, which becomes a leaven for a reconciled world." , 

Addressing global challenges, Leo XIV noted "too much discord, too many wounds caused by hatred, violence, prejudice, the fear of difference, and an economic paradigm that exploits the Earth's resources and marginalizes the poorest" , . He referenced his episcopal motto, *In illo Uno unum* ("In the One, [we are] one"), urging the faithful to become "one family" in Christ , .

He also paid tribute to his predecessor, Pope Francis, stating that during the vacancy of the Holy See, the faithful felt "like sheep without a shepherd," but were sustained by the late pope's final blessing , .

## Attendees

The Vatican reported that approximately 150,000 to 200,000 people attended the Mass in St. Peter's Square and the surrounding area , .

### Official Delegations
Over 100 government delegations and roughly 150 total delegations attended the event , . Notable political figures included:
* **United States:** Vice President JD Vance and Secretary of State Marco Rubio , .
* **Ukraine:** President Volodymyr Zelenskyy , .
* **Peru:** President Dina Boluarte , .
* **Colombia:** President Gustavo Petro .
* **Argentina:** Minister of Foreign Affairs Gerardo Werthein .

### Religious Representatives
Ecumenical and interfaith relations were a significant aspect of the attendance. Bartholomew I, the Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople, was present, continuing the tradition of close relations between the Holy See and the Orthodox Church , . Representatives from the Anglican Communion, the Lutheran World Federation, the World Methodist Council, and various Evangelical and Pentecostal communities also attended .

Delegations from non-Christian faiths were also present, including representatives from the Jewish, Muslim, Hindu, Buddhist, Sikh, Zoroastrian, and Jain communities , .

## Post-Inauguration Events

Following the Mass, Pope Leo XIV greeted the heads of state and government delegations inside St. Peter's Basilica . On May 19, the day after the inauguration, he held private audiences with specific leaders, including U.S. Vice President JD Vance, who presented the pope with a Chicago Bears jersey bearing the name "Pope Leo" and the number "XIV" .

### Possession of the Basilicas
As is custom, the new pope took formal possession of the major basilicas of Rome in the days following the inauguration:
* **May 20, 2025:** Basilica of Saint Paul Outside the Walls , .
* **May 25, 2025:** Archbasilica of Saint John Lateran (the cathedral of the Bishop of Rome) and the Basilica of Santa Maria Maggiore , .

## Misinformation and Deepfakes
In the weeks surrounding the election and inauguration, the Vatican contended with a proliferation of AI-generated deepfake videos depicting Pope Leo XIV , . These videos included fabricated footage of the pope making controversial political statements, praising military leaders in Burkina Faso, and resigning from the papacy , , . The Vatican's Dicastery for Communication issued warnings regarding these fabrications, and the pope himself addressed the issue of artificial intelligence, calling for ethical governance of the technology , , .

**Hoax – Pope Leo XIV allegedly made a dramatic confession, leaving the Vatican after revealing he had a son he had abandoned for over thirty years. Afterward, he resigned.**

Analysis

A video with highly dramatic and personal content has generated great repercussions and raised questions among the faithful and the general public. The images circulating on the internet show what is allegedly a surprising “confession” from the current Pope, Leo XIV, elected in May 2025.

In the recording, the highest authority of the Catholic Church is supposedly breaking the silence about a decades-old secret, which led him to abandon the Vatican. The narrative of a crisis of conscience and the theme of secret paternity, in contrast to the celibacy required by religious life, naturally catapulted the story to massive reach on social media. Read:

Version 1: _IF TRUE, WOULD THE POPE’S PUBLIC CONFESSION REALLY BE MERITORIOUS? To a non-Catholic, as is my case, the video in which Pope Leo XIV allegedly admits to having had a sexual involvement with a woman, which resulted in a son, whom he abandoned for thirty-two years, is a warning about the power of Artificial Intelligence (AI) to cause changes even within an institution whose sluggishness, despite its eagerness for “aggiornamento” in the face of contemporary values, is as ambiguous as it is proverbial! The official website of the Holy See and several fact-checking agencies (such as major international news outlets and global fact-checkers) have already confirmed that this and other similar videos are “deepfakes,” created with the strategic intention of disseminating misinformation, perhaps aiming, I believe, to force the debate about celibacy._

_At first glance, the content even seems authentic and true, because it uses real images of the Pope, but, above all, the extremely frank discourse, in flagrant contradiction with the traditional discretion with which, on delicate issues of a moral and personal nature, the Vatican, fearful of scandal, always tries to preserve the members of its high-ranking hierarchy, is neither convincing nor coherent, the paradoxical disclosure of an unusual public unburdening by its highest authority, which reinforces the conviction that it is a montage. Pope Leo XIV (Robert Francis Prevost), who was recently elected in May 2025, did in fact consider getting married and having children in his youth, before entering religious life, a fact that is mentioned in his official biography. However, he did not have children and the video in question is a fraud, part of a wave of false content about the new pontiff that flooded the internet after his election._

Version 2: _I can no longer remain silent | Pope Leo XIV abandons the Vatican and reveals a secret that changes everything In this absolutely revealing video, you will discover why Pope Leo XIV finally decided to break the silence and abandon the Vatican after receiving a spiritual message that, according to him, will change everything we know about faith, the future of the Church, and the prophetic events that have already begun to be fulfilled. This is not a common statement — it is an urgent call, a direct warning, an alert that no Christian can ignore. Here, you will understand the secret that was hidden for decades within the walls of the Vatican and that now comes to light at a critical moment for humanity. Prepare yourself: this message is strong, profound, and can transform your spiritual vision. Watch until the end and share this revelation with those you love._

Fact Check

Despite the intense circulation and the shocking nature of the video, a detailed investigation into the material and its context reveals that the story is nothing more than fake news. To answer readers’ questions, we checked the following issues: 1) Did Pope Leo XIV really reveal he had a son and resign from his post in the Vatican? 2) How was the video that claims Pope Leo XIV reveals he has a son and resigns from his post in the Vatican made? 3) Are there other similar fake news stories about the pontiff?

No, Pope Leo XIV did not reveal he had a son nor did he resign from his post in the Vatican. The Supreme Pontiff, which is the name given to [Robert Francis Prevost](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papa_Le%C3%A3o_XIV), remains in his position and there is no official record or statement from the Holy See confirming the facts narrated in the video.

The rumor uses a narrative of dramatic confession and abandonment of power to generate commotion, but it is completely disconnected from reality. The official Vatican website and credible international news agencies have not published anything about such a resignation or confession, which would be an event of global impact.

How was the video that claims Pope Leo XIV reveals he has a son and resigns from his post in the Vatican made?
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The video in question is a deepfake production, meaning manipulated and synthetic content created by Artificial Intelligence. Although the video may use authentic images of the Pope, the audio and, consequently, the confession, are falsified.

Are there other similar fake news stories about the pontiff?
------------------------------------------------------------

Yes, Pope Leo XIV has been a constant target of a series of [fake news stories created using AI](https://www.boatos.org/lista/top-5-fake-news-criadas-com-ia-sobre-o-papa-leao-xiv.html) since his election. The dissemination of false content seems to be part of a coordinated strategy to misinform the public and, possibly, to force a debate on sensitive issues for the Church, such as the question of celibacy.

[Boatos.org](https://www.boatos.org/), for example, has already cataloged other false narratives about the pontiff, such as one accusing him of silencing an atheist professor in a university debate, which also proved [to be a fraud](https://www.boatos.org/religiao/papa-leao-xiv-silenciou-professor-ateu-em-debate-universitario.html). This wave of misinformation highlights the importance of fact-checking before sharing any material of dubious origin.

Conclusion

The video that attributes the confession of having a son and the subsequent resignation from the papacy to Pope Leo XIV is a piece of misinformation. It is a highly manipulated deepfake created by Artificial Intelligence, which uses the real figure of the pontiff to disseminate a fictional and dramatic story. Pope Leo XIV made no such confession and remains in charge of the Vatican, with the narrative being part of a wave of false content created to distort the reality about the new leader of the Catholic Church.

Fake news ❌

**Who is Robert Prevost, the man who is now Leo XIV?**  
  
What personal traits led him to be chosen as pontiff at a time when the Catholic Church was debating whether to continue the legacy of Francis I or roll back the reforms advanced by him? How did he rise as pope in an overwhelmingly majority vote and what could it mean?  
  
Elise Ann Allen, correspondent in Rome for Crux, the prestigious website specialising in Vatican news, outlines a detailed and intimate profile of the new pope. From his childhood in Chicago and his early vocation as an Augustinian to his years as a missionary in Peru and his key role in the Vatican as head of the bishops, Allen reveals the experiences that forged his character and established him as a spiritual leader and citizen of the world.  
  
Including the first interview that Leo XIV officially granted as pope, this biography is essential reading for anyone seeking to understand the new pope**,** his priorities, convictions and vision for the future of the Church.

Read more

About Elise Ann Allen
---------------------

**Elise Ann Allen** is a correspondent in Rome for the specialised media outlet Crux. Before joining Crux, Elise worked with Catholic News Agency, first as a multi-media and content management assistant in Denver. She holds a degree in Philosophy and Communications from the University of Northern Colorado.

Click here for more information.") From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia
Inauguration of Pope Leo XIV

St. Peter's Square during the liturgy

Native nameCelebrazione Eucaristica per l'Inizio del Ministero del Vescovo di Roma
English nameEucharistic Celebration for the Beginning of the Ministry of the Bishop of Rome
Date18 May 2025
Time10 a.m. (CEST, UTC+02:00)
VenueSt. Peter's Square
LocationVatican City
TypePapal inauguration
Participants200,000
On 18 May 2025, [Pope Leo XIV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV "Pope Leo XIV") celebrated the [inauguration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papal_inauguration "Papal inauguration") Mass of his pontificate, formally known as the "Mass for the Beginning of the Petrine Ministry of the Bishop of Rome".[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papal_inauguration_of_Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Pillar-1) The event was attended by some 200,000 people, including dozens of world leaders and 150 formal delegations.[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papal_inauguration_of_Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Bigg-2) While Leo became the Roman pontiff at the moment of his acceptance in the [Sistine Chapel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sistine_Chapel "Sistine Chapel") upon being elected in the [2025 papal conclave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_papal_conclave "2025 papal conclave"), the inauguration celebration marked the formal beginning of his ministry as the [bishop of Rome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bishop_of_Rome "Bishop of Rome").[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papal_inauguration_of_Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Pillar-1) The Mass included the bestowal of the [pallium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pallium "Pallium") and [Ring of the Fisherman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ring_of_the_Fisherman "Ring of the Fisherman"), and was followed by meetings with various delegations and world leaders. [![Image 3](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/87/Leone_XIV_-_18-05-2025.jpg/250px-Leone_XIV_-_18-05-2025.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Leone_XIV_-_18-05-2025.jpg) Leo blessing and greeting crowds in the [popemobile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Popemobile "Popemobile") prior to the ceremony [![Image 4](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/6e/Coat_of_arms_of_Leone_XIV.svg/250px-Coat_of_arms_of_Leone_XIV.svg.png)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Coat_of_arms_of_Leone_XIV.svg) Pope Leo XIV's [coat of arms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coat_of_arms "Coat of arms") Prior to the ceremony, Leo toured [St. Peter's Square](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Peter%27s_Square "St. Peter's Square") in the [popemobile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Popemobile "Popemobile") for the first time, where attendees shouted __Viva il Papa_!_ (Long live the Pope),[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papal_inauguration_of_Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Pillar-1) and "[USA, USA!](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U-S-A! "U-S-A!")"[\[3\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papal_inauguration_of_Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-3) with at least one person chanting "[White Sox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Sox "White Sox")!",[\[4\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papal_inauguration_of_Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Anderson-4) referencing his country of birth and favorite baseball team.[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papal_inauguration_of_Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Pillar-1) Others waved [Peruvian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flag_of_Peru "Flag of Peru") or American flags for the countries that claim him as a citizen.[\[5\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papal_inauguration_of_Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-5) The liturgy formally began at 10 a.m. at [Saint Peter's tomb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint_Peter%27s_tomb "Saint Peter's tomb") underneath [the baldachin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Peter%27s_Baldachin "St. Peter's Baldachin") of the high altar of [St. Peter's Basilica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Peter%27s_Basilica "St. Peter's Basilica"). Surrounded by the [patriarchs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patriarch "Patriarch") of the [Eastern Catholic Churches](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Catholic_Churches "Eastern Catholic Churches"), Leo incensed the tomb while the choir sang __Tu es Petrus__, a [motet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Motet "Motet") by [Giovanni Pierluigi da Palestrina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giovanni_Pierluigi_da_Palestrina "Giovanni Pierluigi da Palestrina"). Ascending from the grottoes, Leo was joined in procession to the square by two deacons holding the [Ring of the Fisherman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ring_of_the_Fisherman "Ring of the Fisherman") and the papal [pallium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pallium "Pallium"), as well as cardinals and bishops. The traditional _[Laudes Regiae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laudes_Regiae "Laudes Regiae")_ chant was sung during the procession. Leo then conducted the [asperges](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asperges "Asperges") rite, typical on Sundays of [Eastertide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastertide "Eastertide").[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papal_inauguration_of_Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Pillar-1) [![Image 5](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7b/Pope_Leo_XIV_Inauguration.jpg/250px-Pope_Leo_XIV_Inauguration.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Pope_Leo_XIV_Inauguration.jpg) Leo in front of the altar The first reading, from [Acts 4:8-12](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acts_4 "Acts 4"), was proclaimed in Spanish, referencing Leo's work in the [Diocese of Chiclayo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diocese_of_Chiclayo "Diocese of Chiclayo"). [Psalm 118](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Psalm_118 "Psalm 118") was sung in Italian, for his new [diocese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diocese_of_Rome "Diocese of Rome"); the second reading, from [1 Peter 5:1-5, 10-11](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1_Peter_5 "1 Peter 5"), was proclaimed in English by a faculty member from the [Pontifical North American College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pontifical_North_American_College "Pontifical North American College"), referencing Leo's native tongue. The Gospel, [John 21:15-19](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Restoration_of_Peter "Restoration of Peter"), was chanted in Latin by a deacon from the [Diocese of Fort Wayne–South Bend](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roman_Catholic_Diocese_of_Fort_Wayne%E2%80%93South_Bend "Roman Catholic Diocese of Fort Wayne–South Bend"), Indiana, then subsequently chanted in Greek.[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papal_inauguration_of_Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Pillar-1)[\[6\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papal_inauguration_of_Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Vatican_News_2025-6) Representing the [cardinal deacons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_/(Catholic_Church/)#Cardinal_deacons "Cardinal (Catholic Church)"), [Mario Zenari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Zenari "Mario Zenari") imposed the [pallium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pallium "Pallium") on Leo's shoulders. Then, representing the [cardinal priests](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_/(Catholic_Church/)#Cardinal_priests "Cardinal (Catholic Church)"), [Fridolin Ambongo Besungu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fridolin_Ambongo_Besungu "Fridolin Ambongo Besungu") conferred a prayer of blessing on the pope. Finally, [Luis Antonio Tagle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Antonio_Tagle "Luis Antonio Tagle"), for [cardinal bishops](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_/(Catholic_Church/)#Cardinal_bishops "Cardinal (Catholic Church)"), bestowed the [Ring of the Fisherman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ring_of_the_Fisherman "Ring of the Fisherman") upon the pontiff;[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papal_inauguration_of_Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Pillar-1) Leo appeared visibly moved by the moment.[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papal_inauguration_of_Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Pillar-1)[\[4\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papal_inauguration_of_Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Anderson-4) Following the investment of the insignia, twelve delegates representing the Catholic Church from around the world, including clerics, vowed religious, a married couple, and young adults, were received by Leo. The homily delivered by Leo followed, where he spoke in Italian.[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papal_inauguration_of_Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Pillar-1) The prayers of the faithful were delivered in Arabic, Chinese, French, Polish, and Portuguese. __Tu es pastor ovium__ was chanted during the offertory. Leo prayed the [Roman Canon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roman_Canon "Roman Canon").[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papal_inauguration_of_Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Pillar-1) Before the conclusion of Mass, Leo offered some brief remarks, especially offering prayers for the [conflicts in Gaza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza%E2%80%93Israel_conflict "Gaza–Israel conflict"), [Myanmar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Myanmar_civil_war_/(2021%E2%80%93present/) "Myanmar civil war (2021–present)"), and [Ukraine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_invasion_of_Ukraine "Russian invasion of Ukraine"). The _[Regina cæli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Regina_Caeli "Regina Caeli")_ was sung, followed by the final blessing.[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papal_inauguration_of_Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Pillar-1) Some 30 heads of state, 200 cardinals, and 750 bishops and priests were present.[\[7\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papal_inauguration_of_Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-7) Throughout the ceremony, Leo used the [papal ferula](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papal_ferula "Papal ferula") commonly used by [Pope John Paul II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_John_Paul_II "Pope John Paul II").[\[8\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papal_inauguration_of_Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-8) Princess [Charlene of Monaco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlene_of_Monaco "Charlene of Monaco"), Queen [Letizia of Spain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Letizia_of_Spain "Letizia of Spain"), Queen [Mathilde of Belgium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathilde_of_Belgium "Mathilde of Belgium"), and Grand Duchess [Maria Teresa of Luxembourg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maria_Teresa,_Grand_Duchess_of_Luxembourg "Maria Teresa, Grand Duchess of Luxembourg") exercised the _[privilège du blanc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Privil%C3%A8ge_du_blanc "Privilège du blanc")_ extended to Catholic royalty by wearing white to the ceremony.[\[9\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papal_inauguration_of_Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-9)[\[10\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papal_inauguration_of_Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-10) Leo began his sermon by thanking those who were present and remembering the emotions of the previous weeks following the [death of Pope Francis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Death_of_Pope_Francis "Death of Pope Francis") and [subsequent conclave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_papal_conclave "2025 papal conclave"). Recalling the two-fold aspects of ministry entrusted to [Saint Peter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint_Peter "Saint Peter"), love and unity, Leo said he would approach the Church as a brother and servant and with "[fear and trembling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fear_and_trembling_/(biblical_phrase/) "Fear and trembling (biblical phrase)")".[\[11\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papal_inauguration_of_Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-VN-11) Leo expressed a desire for unity and communion in the Church and in the world.[\[4\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papal_inauguration_of_Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Anderson-4) He condemned exploitation of Earth's resources and marginalization of the poor.[\[11\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papal_inauguration_of_Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-VN-11) He referenced his [papal motto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coat_of_arms_of_Pope_Leo_XIV "Coat of arms of Pope Leo XIV"), "in the one Christ, we are one", and exclaimed "Look to Christ! Come closer to him!"[\[11\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papal_inauguration_of_Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-VN-11)[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papal_inauguration_of_Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Pillar-1) Subsequent activities --------------------- \[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Papal_inauguration_of_Pope_Leo_XIV&action=edit§ion=4 "Edit section: Subsequent activities")\] After the ceremony, Leo entered St. Peter's basilica and met with 150 delegations in front of the St. Peter's baldachin.[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papal_inauguration_of_Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Pillar-1) Among the delegations was [his brother Louis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Family_of_Pope_Leo_XIV "Family of Pope Leo XIV"), whom he embraced.[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papal_inauguration_of_Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Bigg-2) After the inauguration, Leo met with Peruvian president [Dina Boluarte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dina_Boluarte "Dina Boluarte")[\[12\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papal_inauguration_of_Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-12) and Ukrainian president [Volodymyr Zelenskyy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy "Volodymyr Zelenskyy").[\[13\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papal_inauguration_of_Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-13) On Monday, 19 May, Leo met with US Vice President [JD Vance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JD_Vance "JD Vance") and Secretary of State [Marco Rubio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marco_Rubio "Marco Rubio"). Vance appeared to give Leo a [Chicago Bears](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Bears "Chicago Bears") jersey with the name "Pope Leo" and number "XIV".[\[14\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papal_inauguration_of_Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-14) Leo also met with [Gustavo Petro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gustavo_Petro "Gustavo Petro"), president of Colombia;[\[15\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papal_inauguration_of_Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-15) [Bartholomew](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bartholomew_I_of_Constantinople "Bartholomew I of Constantinople"), the [ecumenical patriarch of Constantinople](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ecumenical_patriarch_of_Constantinople "Ecumenical patriarch of Constantinople");[\[16\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papal_inauguration_of_Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-16) [Gerardo Werthein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gerardo_Werthein "Gerardo Werthein"), Minister of Foreign Affairs and Worship of Argentina; and representatives of other churches, ecclesiastical communities, and religions.[\[17\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papal_inauguration_of_Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-17) In the days following the inauguration, Leo took possession of the other [major basilicas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_basilica "Major basilica"), with ceremonies held at the [Basilica of Saint Paul Outside the Walls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basilica_of_Saint_Paul_Outside_the_Walls "Basilica of Saint Paul Outside the Walls") on 20 May, and at the [Archbasilica of Saint John Lateran](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archbasilica_of_Saint_John_Lateran "Archbasilica of Saint John Lateran") and the Basilica of [Santa Maria Maggiore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Maria_Maggiore "Santa Maria Maggiore") on 25 May, formally installing him as the Bishop of Rome.[\[18\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papal_inauguration_of_Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-18)[\[19\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papal_inauguration_of_Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-19) Official delegations **Papal inauguration** is a [liturgical service](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liturgy "Liturgy") of the [Catholic Church](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catholic_Church "Catholic Church") within [Mass](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mass_/(liturgy/) "Mass (liturgy)") celebrated in the [Roman Rite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roman_Rite "Roman Rite") but with elements of [Byzantine Rite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Byzantine_Rite "Byzantine Rite") for the ecclesiastical [investiture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Investiture "Investiture") of a [pope](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope "Pope"). Since the [inauguration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papal_inauguration_of_Pope_John_Paul_I "Papal inauguration of Pope John Paul I") of [Pope John Paul I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_John_Paul_I "Pope John Paul I"), it has not included the 820-year-old (1143–1963) [papal coronation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papal_coronation "Papal coronation") ceremony.

It was in the 11th century that the inauguration took the form of a [coronation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coronation "Coronation").[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papal_inauguration#cite_note-1) Along with other ceremonies used at papal inaugurations,[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papal_inauguration#cite_note-2)[\[3\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papal_inauguration#cite_note-3) a coronation became part of a pope's inauguration ritual from the time of [Pope Nicholas II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Nicholas_II "Pope Nicholas II") (1059–1061)[\[4\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papal_inauguration#cite_note-4) until 1963. [Pope Paul VI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Paul_VI "Pope Paul VI"), the last pope to be crowned or to use a [papal tiara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papal_tiara "Papal tiara"), abandoned the use of his tiara in a ceremony at the end of the second period of the [Second Vatican Council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Vatican_Council "Second Vatican Council").

[More than twenty tiaras](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_papal_tiaras_in_existence "List of papal tiaras in existence") are held in the Vatican. That of Paul VI is in the crypt of the [Basilica of the National Shrine of the Immaculate Conception](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basilica_of_the_National_Shrine_of_the_Immaculate_Conception "Basilica of the National Shrine of the Immaculate Conception") in [Washington, D.C.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington,_D.C. "Washington, D.C.")

A small one is still used to symbolically crown a statue of [Saint Peter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint_Peter "Saint Peter") on his saint's day every year. The first pope for more than eight centuries to inaugurate his pontificate without a coronation was [Pope John Paul I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_John_Paul_I "Pope John Paul I").

Abandonment of the coronation
-----------------------------

\[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Papal_inauguration&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Abandonment of the coronation")\]

[Pope Paul VI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Paul_VI "Pope Paul VI"), the last pope to be crowned or to use a [papal tiara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papal_tiara "Papal tiara"), abandoned the use of his tiara in a ceremony at the end of the second period of the [Second Vatican Council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Vatican_Council "Second Vatican Council"), and announced that it would be sold and the money obtained would be given to charity; it was in fact bought by Catholics in the [United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States "United States") and is now kept in the [Basilica of the National Shrine of the Immaculate Conception](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basilica_of_the_National_Shrine_of_the_Immaculate_Conception "Basilica of the National Shrine of the Immaculate Conception") in [Washington, D.C.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington,_D.C. "Washington, D.C.")[\[5\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papal_inauguration#cite_note-5)

Though Paul VI decided not to wear a tiara, his 1975 [apostolic constitution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apostolic_constitution "Apostolic constitution") _[Romano Pontifici eligendo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romano_Pontifici_eligendo "Romano Pontifici eligendo")_ continued to envisage a "coronation" ceremony for his successors. However, [Pope John Paul I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_John_Paul_I "Pope John Paul I"), elected in the [August 1978 conclave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papal_conclave,_1978_/(August/) "Papal conclave, 1978 (August)"), wanted a simpler ceremony, and commissioned [Virgilio Noè](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virgilio_No%C3%A8 "Virgilio Noè"), the Papal [Master of Ceremonies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Master_of_Ceremonies "Master of Ceremonies"), to design the inauguration ceremony that was used. Taking place in the context of a "Mass of Inauguration", the high point of the ceremony was the placing of the [pallium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pallium "Pallium") on the new pope's shoulders, and the receiving of the obedience of the [cardinals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_/(Catholic/) "Cardinal (Catholic)").

His successor, [Pope John Paul II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_John_Paul_II "Pope John Paul II"), followed suit, maintaining the changes made by his predecessor, though with additions. The Mass of inauguration was celebrated, not in the evening, as for John Paul I, but in the morning. Referring in his inauguration [homily](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homily "Homily") to coronation with the papal tiara, John Paul II said: "This is not the time to return to a ceremony and an object considered, wrongly, to be a symbol of the [temporal power](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Temporal_power_/(Papal/) "Temporal power (Papal)") of the Popes."

In his 1996 apostolic constitution _[Universi Dominici gregis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universi_Dominici_gregis "Universi Dominici gregis")_, John Paul II laid down that a "solemn ceremony of the inauguration of a pontificate" should take place, but did not specify its form, which he left to each pope to decide.

Modern papal inauguration
-------------------------

\[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Papal_inauguration&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Modern papal inauguration")\]

Five modern popes have now used an inauguration ceremony without coronation: [Pope John Paul I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_John_Paul_I "Pope John Paul I"), [Pope John Paul II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_John_Paul_II "Pope John Paul II") (both in 1978), [Pope Benedict XVI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Benedict_XVI "Pope Benedict XVI") (2005), [Pope Francis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Francis "Pope Francis") (2013), and [Pope Leo XIV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV "Pope Leo XIV") (2025).

The modern papal inauguration, developed from the form used for John Paul I, takes place during [Mass](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mass_/(liturgy/) "Mass (liturgy)") (usually in [Saint Peter's Square](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint_Peter%27s_Square "Saint Peter's Square")) and involves the formal bestowal of the [pallium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pallium "Pallium"), the symbol of the pope's universal jurisdiction, on the newly elected pope by the senior [Cardinal Deacon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Deacon "Cardinal Deacon").\[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_\]

Pope Benedict XVI maintained those changes and also shortened, as explained below, the ceremony of homage previously paid at a papal inauguration by each cardinal individually, repeating the "act of homage and obedience" made in the conclave to the new pope before the announcement of his election to the people.[\[6\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papal_inauguration#cite_note-6)

The ceremony does not include the alleged [Papal Oath](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papal_profession_of_faith_/(late_7th_century/) "Papal profession of faith (late 7th century)") that some [traditionalist Catholics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Traditionalist_Catholic "Traditionalist Catholic") claim, without evidence, to have been sworn by the popes before John Paul I. They criticise its absence, and some [sedevacantist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sedevacantism "Sedevacantism") groups refuse to accept the legitimacy of the modern popes due to the absence of both the alleged oath and the symbolic tiara.[\[7\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papal_inauguration#cite_note-7)

Inauguration of Benedict XVI
----------------------------

\[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Papal_inauguration&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Inauguration of Benedict XVI")\]

[![Image 1](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1f/Benedikt_XVI_im_Papamobil.jpg/250px-Benedikt_XVI_im_Papamobil.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Benedikt_XVI_im_Papamobil.jpg)

Pope Benedict XVI's first trip in the [popemobile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Popemobile "Popemobile") at his inauguration

[Pope Benedict XVI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Benedict_XVI "Pope Benedict XVI") celebrated his inauguration on 24 April 2005 after being elected on 19 April 2005 having approved new procedures for the papal inauguration previously on 20 April 2005 the day after his election. The ceremony began with the pope and the cardinals kneeling at the [Tomb of Saint Peter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint_Peter%27s_tomb "Saint Peter's tomb") beneath the high altar of [Saint Peter's Basilica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint_Peter%27s_Basilica "Saint Peter's Basilica")—the popes are, according to Catholic dogma, the successors of [Saint Peter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint_Peter "Saint Peter"), the first head of the Church in Rome—to give him homage, and ask his prayers. Pope Benedict said, "I leave from where the Apostle arrived." The pope and the cardinals then went in procession to Saint Peter's Square for the inauguration Mass, while the _[Laudes Regiæ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laudes_Regi%C3%A6 "Laudes Regiæ")_ was chanted, asking help for the new pope.

### Receiving the pallium and the Piscatory Ring

\[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Papal_inauguration&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Receiving the pallium and the Piscatory Ring")\]

The pope received the [pallium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pallium "Pallium") and the [Ring of the Fisherman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ring_of_the_Fisherman "Ring of the Fisherman"). Cardinal [Jorge Medina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jorge_Medina_/(cardinal/) "Jorge Medina (cardinal)"), the cardinal protodeacon, formally bestowed the pallium on the pope.[\[8\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papal_inauguration#cite_note-Benedictinauguration-8) The pallium used was different from that of previous popes: it was an earlier form practically identical to the ancient [omophorion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Omophorion "Omophorion") (still used to this day by Eastern bishops); wider than the standard [archiepiscopal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archbishop "Archbishop") pallium, though not as wide as the modern omophorion; 2.4 metres (2.6 yd) long, made of [wool](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wool "Wool") with black silk tips. It had five embroidered red silk crosses instead of the six black ones of the normal archbishops' pallium. Pope Benedict later in his pontificate would use a pallium similar to that of his immediate predecessors, but with a longer, wider cut and six red crosses.

After the pallium was bestowed and before the Ring of the Fisherman was presented, Cardinal [Stephen Kim Sou-hwan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Kim_Sou-hwan "Stephen Kim Sou-hwan"), as the senior cardinal-priest, pronounced the formal prayer for the new pope.[\[8\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papal_inauguration#cite_note-Benedictinauguration-8)

Cardinal [Angelo Sodano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angelo_Sodano "Angelo Sodano"), as the vice dean of the college of cardinals and secretary of state, formally presented the Ring of the Fisherman to the pope.[\[8\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papal_inauguration#cite_note-Benedictinauguration-8) As the pope himself was the dean, he put on the ring by himself.

Instead of having each of the more than one hundred [cardinals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_/(Catholicism/) "Cardinal (Catholicism)") kneel before the pope individually to do him homage, twelve people, lay as well as clerical, did so: Senior [Cardinal Bishop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Bishop "Cardinal Bishop") [Angelo Sodano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angelo_Sodano "Angelo Sodano"), [Cardinal Protopriest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protopriest "Protopriest") [Stephen Kim Sou-hwan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Kim_Sou-hwan "Stephen Kim Sou-hwan"), [Cardinal Protodeacon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Protodeacon "Cardinal Protodeacon") Jorge Medina, Bishop Andrea Erba of Benedict's former [suburbicarian diocese of Velletri-Segni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suburbicarian_diocese_of_Velletri-Segni "Suburbicarian diocese of Velletri-Segni"), Father Enrico Pomili from Benedict's former [titular church](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Titular_church "Titular church") [Santa Maria Consolatrice al Tiburtino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Maria_Consolatrice_al_Tiburtino "Santa Maria Consolatrice al Tiburtino") when he was a cardinal priest, a [deacon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deacon "Deacon"), a religious brother, a [Benedictine nun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Order_of_Saint_Benedict "Order of Saint Benedict"), a married couple from [Korea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Korea "Korea"), a young woman from [Sri Lanka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sri_Lanka "Sri Lanka"), and a young man from the [Democratic Republic of the Congo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_Republic_of_the_Congo "Democratic Republic of the Congo"), each of whom had been recently [confirmed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Confirmation_/(Catholic_Church/) "Confirmation (Catholic Church)").[\[8\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papal_inauguration#cite_note-Benedictinauguration-8)[\[9\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papal_inauguration#cite_note-9)

After Mass, Pope Benedict greeted inside St. Peter's Basilica, before the main altar, various delegations present for his inauguration. In the days following, he visited the other [major basilicas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_basilica "Major basilica") of Rome. On 25 April 2005, the day after his inauguration at St. Peter's, he paid homage to the other founder of the church of Rome by visiting [St. Paul Outside the Walls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basilica_of_Saint_Paul_Outside_the_Walls "Basilica of Saint Paul Outside the Walls"). On 7 May, he took possession of the [Archbasilica of St. John Lateran](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archbasilica_of_St._John_Lateran "Archbasilica of St. John Lateran")—his cathedral church. Later that evening he venerated the _Salus Populi Romani_ icon of Mary in the [Basilica of Saint Mary Major](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basilica_di_Santa_Maria_Maggiore "Basilica di Santa Maria Maggiore").

Inauguration of Francis
-----------------------

\[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Papal_inauguration&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Inauguration of Francis")\]

[![Image 2](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b5/Francis_Inauguration_fc10.jpg/250px-Francis_Inauguration_fc10.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Francis_Inauguration_fc10.jpg)

Inauguration of Pope Francis

Pope Francis celebrated his papal inauguration on 19 March 2013, the [Solemnity of Saint Joseph](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solemnity_of_Saint_Joseph "Solemnity of Saint Joseph"), following his election on 13 March 2013. He used a [mitre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mitre "Mitre") he has had since he first became a bishop. His [chasuble](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chasuble "Chasuble") matched the mitre. He used the same [pastoral staff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papal_ferula "Papal ferula") that [Benedict XVI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Benedict_XVI "Pope Benedict XVI") used. Pope Francis kept the chants and liturgical actions simple. The fact that he himself did not chant the liturgy was attributed by Cardinal [Timothy Dolan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timothy_Dolan "Timothy Dolan") to his having only one lung.[\[10\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papal_inauguration#cite_note-10)

Francis first descended to the tomb of St. Peter in St. Peter's Basilica where, along with the [patriarchs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patriarch "Patriarch") and [major-archbishops](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_archbishop "Major archbishop") of the [Eastern Catholic Churches](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Catholic_Churches "Eastern Catholic Churches"), he prayed at the tomb.[\[11\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papal_inauguration#cite_note-Inauguration_video-11) The pallium and the Ring of the Fisherman were then carried up from the tomb by two deacons to be borne in procession.[\[11\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papal_inauguration#cite_note-Inauguration_video-11) The pope and the Eastern Catholic patriarchs and major-archbishops returned to the main floor of the basilica and processed along with the other cardinals, bishops and other clergy to the square, chanting the _Laudes Regiae_.[\[11\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papal_inauguration#cite_note-Inauguration_video-11)

Cardinal [Protodeacon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protodeacon "Protodeacon") [Jean-Louis Tauran](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jean-Louis_Tauran "Jean-Louis Tauran") bestowed the [pallium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pallium "Pallium") on the pope.[\[11\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papal_inauguration#cite_note-Inauguration_video-11) The most senior elector from the cardinal-priests present, [Godfried Daneels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Godfried_Daneels "Godfried Daneels"), read aloud the formal prayer for the new pope before the Ring of the Fisherman was presented.[\[11\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papal_inauguration#cite_note-Inauguration_video-11)[\[a\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papal_inauguration#cite_note-12)[\[12\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papal_inauguration#cite_note-13)[\[13\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papal_inauguration#cite_note-14) [Angelo Sodano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angelo_Sodano "Angelo Sodano"), [Dean of the College of Cardinals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dean_of_the_College_of_Cardinals "Dean of the College of Cardinals"), presented him with his [Fisherman's Ring](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fisherman%27s_Ring "Fisherman's Ring") of gold-plated silver, unlike his predecessors', which were of gold.[\[11\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papal_inauguration#cite_note-Inauguration_video-11)[\[14\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papal_inauguration#cite_note-15) Six cardinals, two of each order, then professed their obedience to Pope Francis on behalf of the [College of Cardinals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/College_of_Cardinals "College of Cardinals"). The six cardinals were [Giovanni Battista Re](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giovanni_Battista_Re "Giovanni Battista Re") and [Tarcisio Bertone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tarcisio_Bertone "Tarcisio Bertone") representing the cardinal-bishops; [Joachim Meisner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joachim_Meisner "Joachim Meisner") and [Jozef Tomko](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jozef_Tomko "Jozef Tomko") representing the cardinal-priests; and [Renato Raffaele Martino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renato_Martino "Renato Martino") and [Francesco Marchisano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Francesco_Marchisano "Francesco Marchisano") representing the cardinal-deacons.[\[11\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papal_inauguration#cite_note-Inauguration_video-11)[\[15\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papal_inauguration#cite_note-16)

Inauguration of Leo XIV
-----------------------

\[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Papal_inauguration&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Inauguration of Leo XIV")\]

[![Image 3](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7b/Pope_Leo_XIV_Inauguration.jpg/250px-Pope_Leo_XIV_Inauguration.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Pope_Leo_XIV_Inauguration.jpg)

Inauguration of Pope Leo XIV

[Pope Leo XIV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV "Pope Leo XIV") held his inauguration on 18 May 2025, the fifth Sunday of Easter, and on the 105th birth anniversary of [Pope St. John Paul II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_John_Paul_II "Pope John Paul II"). He used a white chasuble frequently used by his three predecessors – John Paul II, [Benedict XVI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Benedict_XVI "Pope Benedict XVI") and [Francis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Francis "Pope Francis") – and carried the [Papal ferula](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papal_ferula "Papal ferula"), designed by Lello Scorzelli, used since the time of [Pope Paul VI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Paul_VI "Pope Paul VI"). The [Office for the Liturgical Celebrations of the Supreme Pontiff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Office_for_the_Liturgical_Celebrations_of_the_Supreme_Pontiff "Office for the Liturgical Celebrations of the Supreme Pontiff") released the booklet for the celebration on May 14, 2025, which used the proper prayers and readings for the Inauguration of the Petrine Ministry, instead of the Sunday Readings.[\[16\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papal_inauguration#cite_note-17) The same office provided explanation for the different elements surrounding a Papal Inauguration.[\[17\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papal_inauguration#cite_note-18)

The pope greeted the crowds at [St. Peter's Square](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Peter%27s_Square "St. Peter's Square"), approximately an hour before the beginning of the Mass, going as far as the [Via della Conciliazione](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Via_della_Conciliazione "Via della Conciliazione"), already of Italian territory. He returned back to [St. Peter's Basilica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Peter%27s_Basilica "St. Peter's Basilica") where he, along with the cardinals, and the patriarchs of Eastern Catholic Churches, processed to the Main Altar, where Pope Leo XIV and the Eastern-rite patriarchs prayed before [Saint Peter's tomb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint_Peter%27s_tomb "Saint Peter's tomb"), where the Pallium and Ring of the Fisherman were laid and later taken into procession. The pope and the cardinals processed from the Altar of Confession to [St. Peter's Square](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Peter%27s_Square "St. Peter's Square"), while the hymn _[Laudes Regiae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laudes_Regiae "Laudes Regiae")_ was sung by the choir.

Compared to previous inaugurations, the imposition of the pallium, the prayer for the Pope, and the giving of the [Ring of the Fisherman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ring_of_the_Fisherman "Ring of the Fisherman") was tasked to selected cardinals from each order instead of the senior cardinal from each order. Pope Leo XIV used the same pallium as those used by Metropolitan Archbishops (Pope Benedict XVI and Pope Francis used a modified version of the Pallium, though the latter reverted to the present form in 2014). The ring of the fisherman of Pope Leo XIV bears an image of St. Peter outside, with the coat of arms and his [papal name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papal_name "Papal name") inside, in accordance with tradition.[\[18\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papal_inauguration#cite_note-19) Italian Cardinal [Mario Zenari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Zenari "Mario Zenari"), Apostolic Nuncio to Syria, representing the Cardinal-Deacons and Europe, placed the pallium. Congolese Cardinal [Fridolin Ambongo Besungu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fridolin_Ambongo_Besungu "Fridolin Ambongo Besungu"), archbishop of Kinshasa, representing the Cardinal-Priests and Africa, led the prayer. Filipino Cardinal [Luis Antonio Tagle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Antonio_Tagle "Luis Antonio Tagle"), Pro-Prefect of the [Dicastery for Evangelization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dicastery_for_Evangelization "Dicastery for Evangelization"), representing the cardinal-bishops and Asia, presented the ring to Pope Leo XIV.[\[19\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papal_inauguration#cite_note-20) Similar to Pope Benedict XVI's Inauguration in 2005, the act of homage was represented by selected cardinals, bishops, religious, and lay faithful.

The pope delivered his _[Regina Caeli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Regina_Caeli "Regina Caeli")_ address before the final blessing, appealing for peace in war-torn parts of the world, praying for people suffering because of war, especially in Gaza, Myanmar, and Ukraine.[\[20\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papal_inauguration#cite_note-21) He thanked all participants of the Mass, as well as the official delegations from different parts of the world, along with those participating in the already-scheduled Jubilee of Confraternities of the [2025 Jubilee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Jubilee "2025 Jubilee"). Following the Mass, the pope individually greeted the dignitaries inside St. Peter's Basilica, donning the papal choir dress (stole, mozetta, pectoral cross, and rochet).

_Ad hoc_ rituals were used for the inaugurations of the pontificates of Popes John Paul I and John Paul II. On 20 April 2005, Pope Benedict XVI approved a permanent rite, a draft of which had been made by the Office of Liturgical Celebrations of the Supreme Pontiff under John Paul II. This was published as an official [liturgical book](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liturgical_book "Liturgical book") of the church with the name _Ordo Rituum pro Ministerii Petrini Initio Romae Episcopi_ (Order of the Rites for the Inauguration of the Petrine Ministry of the Bishop of Rome). Archbishop [Piero Marini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piero_Marini "Piero Marini"), the Papal Master of Ceremonies, described it as part of the application to papal rites of the liturgical reforms following the Second Vatican Council.

The _Ordo_ contains not only the text and rubrics for the Mass of the Inauguration, but also of the Mass of the Enthronement on the _cathedra romana_, the physical chair of the pope as Bishop of Rome in the Lateran Basilica, Rome's cathedral and thus the church's only [archbasilica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archbasilica_of_Saint_John_Lateran "Archbasilica of Saint John Lateran") (outranking even Saint Peter's). Popes usually take possession of the Lateran Basilica within a few days of the inauguration of their pontificate.

Shortly before he resigned, Pope Benedict XVI introduced some modifications: strictly non-sacramental ceremonies must not take place within Mass but either before Mass or without Mass; the individual act of homage by each cardinal is restored; a wider choice of music is provided; and the time for taking possession of the basilicas of Saint Paul Outside the Walls and Saint Mary Major is not limited to the two or three weeks following the inauguration.[\[21\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papal_inauguration#cite_note-22)[\[22\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papal_inauguration#cite_note-23)

![Image 1: stpetervatican](https://olmctempe.com/uploads/images/blog/stpetervatican.jpg)

by Fr. Robert Aliunzi  |  05/17/2025  |  Weekly Reflection

Dear Friends,

When the announcement of the new pope was made on May 8th, I was in a hospital bed in the emergency room battling an illness. All of a sudden, my phone went ballistic with messages informing me of who the new pope is - Cardinal Robert Francis Prevost, an American-born Augustinian missionary! What? I unconsciously reacted. At a human level, I was thrilled that the new pope and I both share the name Robert and both of us are Americans of dual citizenship. But I was also shocked, like I believe many were, because though holding a prominent position in the Vatican, little was known about him. Besides, many more still never expected an American to become a pope at this time.

Moreover, when the cardinals entered the conclave, many speculations were already being made about who would most likely emerge as the pope. There were very prominent and popular papabile identified by the secular and ecclesiastical press alike. But many, like me, never expected it to be the little-known Cardinal Robert Francis Prevost who decided to choose the papal name Leo XIV. Since then, the press and many other writers have attempted to offer some glimpses of who the man is. Among the many, I ran across an article about our new pope, which impressed me very much, and I would like to share with you an edited version. It says:

The untold story of newly elected Pope Robert Prevost: In 1975, Robert Prevost was at the top of his game. He was a Chicago math teacher. Devout Catholic. Was accepted into Harvard Law School. He had everything a young man could dream of, but then—he made a decision that no one saw coming. He said no to Harvard. No to a six-figure future. No to fame. No to comfort. And yes—to something few dare to choose: A life of complete surrender. He joined a missionary group and moved to Peru. Not to the cities. Not to the tourist spots.

But to the “most” remote villages—where children die from treatable diseases. And families walk miles just for clean water. There were no roads. No running water. No WiFi. Just mountains. Silence and poverty. But he embraced it like home. Robert didn’t just live “among” the people. He became “one” of them.

*   He learned Quechua—the sacred language of the Incas
*   He carried food on foot for days
*   He slept on dirt floors with the villagers
*   He prayed under the stars

When he wasn’t building shelters, he taught math to barefoot kids under broken rooftops. When he wasn’t teaching, he carried the sick on donkeys to get help. When he wasn’t healing, he listened—truly listened—to stories no one else cared to hear. While his friends from back home became lawyers and doctors, he became something else entirely.

A shepherd.  
A brother.  
A quiet warrior of faith.

And slowly—his legend grew. His acts weren’t broadcast. But they echoed through the Andes. Bishops noticed. Priests noticed.

And eventually—the Vatican noticed. They called him back to lead his entire Augustinian order from serving a village to overseeing 2,800 brothers in over 40 countries.

Still—he kept his same sandals.  
Still—he walked with the poor.  
Still—he rejected luxury.

Then came the call that changed everything: Rome wanted him closer. In 2020, He was appointed Archbishop and assigned to govern other bishops globally. It was rare. But Robert had never chased after tradition (nor fame, they chased after him). He wasn’t just fluent in Latin or Canon Law. He was fluent in “compassion”. In humility. In listening.In “presence”.

The Vatican didn’t just see a priest. They saw a “leader with soul” on September 30, 2023. Pope Francis made it official: Robert Prevost was named a Cardinal. Just one step below the Pope And then… on May 8, 2025

History was made. For the first time, our Pope was:

*   An American.
*   A former math teacher.
*   A missionary to the forgotten who was elevated as the 267th Pope of the Catholic Church

Cardinal Prevost — now Pope Leo XIV proves:

*   Titles mean nothing without service
*   Knowledge is useless without love
*   Faith—without sacrifice—is noise, and sometimes
*   If you turn down the world, you will change it instead

Dear friends, whether this reflects who he is accurately or not, time will tell. But for now, please join me in praying for our Holy Father, Pope Leo XIV. He carries the weight of the Petrine office. He is our beloved shepherd whom the Holy Spirit has gifted us with at this time of the Church’s history. The Holy Spirit never errs in his choice.

Let us pray:

Lord, source of eternal life and truth, give to your shepherd Pope Leo XIV a spirit of courage and right judgment, a spirit of knowledge and love. By governing with fidelity those entrusted to his care, may he build your Church into a sacrament of unity, love, and peace for all the world. Amen!

I love you!
