Views
-----

[![Image 12](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/65/Papa_Leone_XIII_%281898%29.jpg/250px-Papa_Leone_XIII_%281898%29.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Papa_Leone_XIII_/(1898/).jpg)

Prevost chose the papal name Leo in honor of [Pope Leo XIII](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIII "Pope Leo XIII")'s social teachings.

Prevost's [regnal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papal_name "Papal name") name was chosen in honor of [Pope Leo XIII](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIII "Pope Leo XIII") (r. 1878–1903),[\[184\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-194) whose encyclical _[Rerum novarum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rerum_novarum "Rerum novarum")_ established modern [Catholic social teaching](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catholic_social_teaching "Catholic social teaching") and promoted [labor rights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Labor_rights "Labor rights").[\[136\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Galeazzi_2025-145)[\[185\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-195) According to the [Holy See Press Office](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holy_See_Press_Office "Holy See Press Office") director [Matteo Bruni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matteo_Bruni "Matteo Bruni"), this choice is "clearly a reference to the lives of men and women, to their work – even in an age marked by artificial intelligence".[\[186\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-196) Leo XIV confirmed the association with Leo XIII in an address to the [World Meeting of Popular Movements](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Popular_movement "Popular movement") in October 2025.[\[187\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-197)

According to Cardinal [Fernando Chomalí](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fernando_Chomal%C3%AD "Fernando Chomalí") of Chile, Leo told him that the choice of papal name is based on his concern about the world's cultural shifts, a type of [Copernican Revolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copernican_Revolution "Copernican Revolution") involving [artificial intelligence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artificial_intelligence "Artificial intelligence") and [robotics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robotics "Robotics"). Chomalí said: "He was inspired by [Leo XIII](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIII "Pope Leo XIII"), who amid the [Industrial Revolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Industrial_Revolution "Industrial Revolution") wrote _Rerum novarum_ launching an important dialogue between the church and the modern world."[\[188\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-198) Leo himself explained that "the church offers to everyone the treasury of her social teaching in response to [another industrial revolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fourth_Industrial_Revolution "Fourth Industrial Revolution") and to developments in the field of artificial intelligence that pose new challenges for the defense of human dignity, justice, and labor."[\[189\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Kent_2025-199)[\[190\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Winfield_2025-200)[\[191\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-201)

In a May 2023 interview, Prevost stressed the need for prudence and responsibility on using social media to preclude "fueling divisions and controversy" and doing "damage to the communion of the Church".[\[192\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Tornielli_2023-202) This view is in line with his tendency to speak "with caution and great deliberation", as Christopher White, the Vatican correspondent of the _[National Catholic Reporter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Catholic_Reporter "National Catholic Reporter")_, described him.[\[193\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-White_2025-203)

The _National Catholic Reporter_ stated that Leo XIV is committed to [ecumenism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ecumenism "Ecumenism") with other [Christian denominations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christian_denomination "Christian denomination").[\[194\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Reese2025-204) At [his inauguration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papal_inauguration_of_Pope_Leo_XIV "Papal inauguration of Pope Leo XIV"), he referenced "sister Christian churches" and prayed for "a united church, a sign of unity and communion, which becomes a leaven for a reconciled world".[\[195\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Collins2025-205)[\[196\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-WCC2025-206)[\[57\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Gomes2025-61) Leo XIV's first international trip as pontiff was to [Turkey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turkey "Turkey") in November 2025, to celebrate the 1,700th anniversary of the [First Council of Nicaea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Council_of_Nicaea "First Council of Nicaea") with other Christians.[\[194\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Reese2025-204)

Prevost has said religious freedom is "not optional but essential". During an audience with pontifical charity [Aid to the Church in Need](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aid_to_the_Church_in_Need "Aid to the Church in Need"), before the launch of its Religious Freedom in the World Report in October 2025, Leo said that the right to religious freedom is "a cornerstone of any just society, for it safeguards the moral space in which conscience may be formed and exercised", adding that "religious freedom, therefore, is not merely a legal right or a privilege granted to us by governments; it is a foundational condition that makes authentic reconciliation possible."[\[197\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-207)

### Church policy

The new pope's first message emphasized the greeting of peace of the risen Jesus "who gave his life for God's flock", giving "an unarmed and disarming peace".[\[198\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-The_Independent_2025-208) Leo said he wanted to continue the [kerygmatic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerygma "Kerygma") blessing of Pope Francis: "God cares for you, God loves you all, and evil will not prevail! We are all in God's hands."[\[198\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-The_Independent_2025-208) The themes in his first message included Jesus as [light needed by the world](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Light_of_the_World "Light of the World"), becoming a missionary church through dialogue and openness, fidelity to the [Gospel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gospel "Gospel"), walking together in synodality, working as a united church for peace and justice, closeness to the suffering, and [praying to Mary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Veneration_of_Mary_in_the_Catholic_Church "Veneration of Mary in the Catholic Church"). Twice he mentioned the need of not having fear, and emphasized God's help to "build bridges" for "all of us to be one people always in peace."[\[198\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-The_Independent_2025-208)

In his first address as Pope to the cardinals, Leo declared his "complete commitment" to the ecclesial path traced by the [Second Vatican Council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Vatican_Council "Second Vatican Council"). He praised Pope Francis's specification of this path through _[Evangelii Gaudium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evangelii_Gaudium "Evangelii Gaudium")_, the Joy of the Gospel, and highlighted six "evangelical principles", which he deems as perennial and revelatory of [God's mercy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Divine_mercy "Divine mercy"): the [primacy of Christ in proclamation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerygma "Kerygma"); the [missionary conversion of the entire Christian community](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_evangelization "New evangelization"); [collegiality](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Collegiality_in_the_Catholic_Church "Collegiality in the Catholic Church") and synodality; attention to the _[sensus fidei](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sensus_fidei "Sensus fidei")_, the capacity of the whole faithful to sense the faith, especially [popular piety](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Popular_piety "Popular piety"); loving care for the least and the rejected; and dialogue with the contemporary world.[\[199\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-209)[\[200\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-210)

Leo XIV's episcopal motto is _In illo Uno unum_ ("In the One, we are one").[\[12\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Vatican_News_2025-15) On the official start of his pontificate, during the [inaugural Mass](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papal_inauguration_of_Pope_Leo_XIV "Papal inauguration of Pope Leo XIV"), he requested that "our first great desire be for a united Church, a sign of unity and communion, which becomes a leaven for a reconciled world."[\[201\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-211) Noting that there is "too much discord" in the world, he stressed that "the two dimensions of the mission" of the papacy is "love and unity", as its authority is "a question of loving as Jesus did."[\[202\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-212)[\[203\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-213)

Discussing the [ordination of women](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ordination_of_women "Ordination of women") in October 2023, Prevost stated that the "very significant and long tradition of the church" makes it impossible to consider women as priests and that "the apostolic tradition is something that has been spelled out very clearly." By contrast, he observed that the possibility of women deacons has been the subject of two Vatican commissions, demonstrating "openness to giving consideration" to that question. He also cautioned that the ordination of women as deacons "doesn't necessarily solve a problem" and could create new issues.[\[204\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-214)[\[205\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Mares_2023-215)[\[206\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Zagano-2025-216) Commenting on Pope Francis's 2023 appointment of three women as members of the Dicastery for Bishops, which he headed, he noted that their perspectives often align with other members but can introduce new valuable viewpoints.[\[207\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-217)

As a cardinal, Prevost was a vocal proponent of [synodality](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Synodality "Synodality"), one of Pope Francis's signature initiatives. Prevost suggested that the participation and co-responsibility of all the faithful could address the polarization in the church.[\[193\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-White_2025-203) In May 2023, Prevost said that [episcopal leadership](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Episcopal_leadership "Episcopal leadership") should prioritize faith over administration. The first priority is to "communicate the beauty of the faith, the beauty and joy of knowing Jesus."[\[192\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Tornielli_2023-202) Also in May 2023, Prevost said he has faith that "the Holy Spirit is \[...\] pushing us towards a renewal."[\[192\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Tornielli_2023-202) He stated that all the faithful are "called to the great responsibility of living what I call a new attitude," which is "to listen first of all to the Holy Spirit, to what He is asking of the Church."[\[192\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Tornielli_2023-202)

### Liturgical and ceremonial practice

[![Image 13](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/28/Homily_during_the_inauguration_of_Leo_XIV.jpg/250px-Homily_during_the_inauguration_of_Leo_XIV.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Homily_during_the_inauguration_of_Leo_XIV.jpg)

Pope Leo XIV presiding over his inaugural papal Mass

During his service in [Peru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peru "Peru"), Prevost was described as an "impeccable dresser" when it came to celebrating the Mass, wearing full vestments even when summer temperatures rose above 85 °F (about 29 °C) in Chiclayo.[\[60\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Rich,_Dias_&_Horowitz_2025-64)[\[208\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-218)[\[86\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Beltr%C3%A1n-91) Prevost described himself as "very obedient" in liturgical matters, and urged that the liturgy be prepared "in the best way possible."[\[209\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-219) In August 2024, speaking to a Chicago-area parish, Prevost stated that "liturgy needs to be beautiful to help us, to strengthen us in our faith."[\[210\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-220) In his first Mass in the [Sistine Chapel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sistine_Chapel "Sistine Chapel") as pope, he chose to use a [papal ferula](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papal_ferula "Papal ferula"), or ceremonial staff, made for [Benedict XVI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benedict_XVI "Benedict XVI") and seldom used by Francis.[\[211\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-221)[\[212\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-222) The mozzetta worn after his election, and Benedict's ferula signaled to some a "return to normal" in the Holy See following the Francis papacy.[\[213\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-223)[\[214\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-224) However, during his Inauguration Mass in St Peter's Square on May 18, 2025, Leo XIV used the ferula of Pope Paul VI which is most commonly associated with Pope John Paul II, and frequently used by Francis.[\[215\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-225)[\[216\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-226)[\[217\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-227)[\[218\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-228) Pope Leo XIV received another pectoral cross upon his election, which he has been wearing instead of the one he wore during the conclave and his first appearance as pope. This one is silver, with relics of St. [Leo the Great](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_I "Pope Leo I"), St. Augustine, St. [Thomas of Villanova](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_of_Villanova "Thomas of Villanova"), and Blessed [Anselmo Polanco Fontecha](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anselmo_Polanco "es:Anselmo Polanco").[\[219\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-229) He also chose to restore the custom of the Pope himself giving archbishops the [pallium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pallium "Pallium"), which had been altered by Francis in 2015.[\[220\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-230)[\[221\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-231) In September 2025, it was announced that Leo had given permission for the [Tridentine Mass](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tridentine_Mass "Tridentine Mass") to be said in St. Peter's Basilica the following month, the first time such permission had been granted since the promulgation of [Traditionis custodes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Traditionis_custodes "Traditionis custodes") in 2021.[\[222\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-232)[\[223\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-233)

### Social and political issues

#### Overview

Within the context of church politics and theology, Prevost has been seen as a moderate or centrist, neither liberal nor conservative.[\[224\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-234) In April 2025, the Italian newspaper _[la Repubblica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Repubblica "La Repubblica")_ stated that Prevost was seen as a "cosmopolitan and shy figure" who was "appreciated by conservatives and progressives" within the church.[\[225\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-235)[\[k\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-237) In line with the church's official positions, Leo opposes [abortion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catholic_Church_and_abortion "Catholic Church and abortion"), [euthanasia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catholic_views_on_euthanasia "Catholic views on euthanasia"), [same-sex marriage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catholic_Church_and_same-sex_marriage "Catholic Church and same-sex marriage") and the [death penalty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catholic_Church_and_capital_punishment "Catholic Church and capital punishment").[\[227\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-238)

#### Pro-life issues

Leo has [opposed abortion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anti-abortion "Anti-abortion") prior to and during his pontificate.[\[228\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-239) In 2012 stated that "[Western mass media](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_mass_media "Western mass media") is extraordinarily effective in fostering within the general public enormous sympathy for beliefs and practices that are at odds with the Gospel—for example abortion, homosexual lifestyle, euthanasia". He reposted articles from the [Catholic News Agency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catholic_News_Agency "Catholic News Agency"), including one from [Mike Pence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pence "Mike Pence") that was titled "Pence to pro-lifers: Win hearts with [compassion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Compassion "Compassion") and love."[\[229\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-240)

Leo has opposed euthanasia[\[230\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-241) He expressed caution against the [euthanasia policy in Canada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euthanasia_in_Canada "Euthanasia in Canada"). He said that euthanasia, along with abortion, "discard the weakest", and disregard the [value of life](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Right_to_life "Right to life"). He has also stated "We cannot build a just society if we discard the weakest—whether the child in the womb or [the elderly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elder_rights "Elder rights") in their frailty—for they are both gifts from God."[\[231\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-242)

Prevost referred to opposition to the death penalty as [pro-life](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pro-life "Pro-life").[\[232\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-243). This comment drew backlash, including from [conservatives](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conservatives "Conservatives") such as [Matt Walsh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matt_Walsh_/(political_commentator/) "Matt Walsh (political commentator)"), a [political commentator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Political_commentator "Political commentator"), who said it was "a terrible answer".[\[233\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-244)

#### LGBTQ+ issues

Prevost expressed reservations about "sympathy for beliefs and practices that contradict the gospel" and did not fully endorse or reject _[Fiducia supplicans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fiducia_supplicans "Fiducia supplicans")_, a declaration concerning blessings for people in a [same-sex relationship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_relationship "Same-sex relationship"). He stated that national bishops' conferences should "interpret and apply such directives in their local contexts, given cultural differences."[\[234\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-245) [Víctor Manuel Fernández](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/V%C3%ADctor_Manuel_Fern%C3%A1ndez "Víctor Manuel Fernández"), the head of the Vatican doctrine office, told _[Il Messaggero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Il_Messaggero "Il Messaggero")_ in July 2025 that he thought the blessing of those in same-sex unions, which had been approved under Pope Francis, would continue under Pope Leo. In May 2025, Cardinal [Jean-Claude Hollerich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jean-Claude_Hollerich "Jean-Claude Hollerich") told _[La Stampa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Stampa "La Stampa")_ that he believed Leo "might re-interpret" _Fiducia Supplicans,_ but not "abolish" it.[\[235\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-246)[\[236\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-247)

In 2012, Prevost criticized popular culture's sympathy for the "homosexual lifestyle" and same-sex families.[\[133\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Rich_2025-142) In April 2016, he opposed the inclusion of "[gender ideology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gender_ideology "Gender ideology")" in Peruvian primary school curricula,[\[237\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-248) stating it promotes "genders that don't exist".[\[133\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Rich_2025-142) When asked in 2023 by [Catholic News Service](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catholic_News_Service "Catholic News Service") whether his views from 2012 had changed, Prevost said that "many things have changed" and emphasized the church should be more open and welcoming though he cautioned that church doctrine has not changed.[\[238\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-249)[\[239\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-250)

In May 2025, Leo XIV said that it was up to governments to build peaceful societies "above all by investing in the family, founded upon the stable union between a man and a woman."[\[240\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-251) In September 2025, Leo told Reverend [James J. Martin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_J._Martin_/(priest/) "James J. Martin (priest)"), a major advocate for greater LGBTQ+ inclusion in the Church, that he would continue Francis' legacy of welcoming LGBTQ+ people into the Church, with Martin telling [The Associated Press](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Associated_Press "The Associated Press") that their discussion "was very consoling and very encouraging and frankly a lot of fun."[\[241\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-252)

#### Geopolitics

Leo with President of Brazil [Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luiz_In%C3%A1cio_Lula_da_Silva "Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva") in October 2025

During his time in Chiclayo, Prevost remained relatively politically neutral on national issues. However, in the midst of the [Peruvian protests](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peruvian_protests_/(2022%E2%80%932023/) "Peruvian protests (2022–2023)") in 2023, he stated: "The deaths during the protests cause me great sadness and pain \[...\] I asked to stay in Peru; I even made that request to the Holy Father. It wasn't the time to leave."[\[242\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-253) He has also expressed support for the plight of Venezuelan refugees in Peru.[\[243\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-McElwee_2025-254)[\[244\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-255) With regards to [climate change](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Climate_change "Climate change"), Prevost has advocated for stronger church action, stating in a November 2024 seminar that "dominion over nature" should not be "tyrannical".[\[147\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Burga_2025-157) He called for [Environmental protection](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Environmental_protection "Environmental protection"), supporting the installation of [solar panels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solar_panels "Solar panels") and [electric vehicles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electric_vehicles "Electric vehicles").[\[245\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-256)

On geopolitics, Prevost has consistently advocated against armed conflict. He denounced the [Russian invasion of Ukraine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_invasion_of_Ukraine "Russian invasion of Ukraine"), describing it as "a true invasion, imperialist in nature, where Russia seeks to conquer territory for reasons of power",[\[246\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-257) and in one of his first major speeches as pope, Leo called for a ceasefire in the [Gaza war](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_war "Gaza war"),[\[247\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-258)[\[248\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-259)[\[249\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-260) later describing Trump's then-proposed [Gaza peace plan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_peace_plan "Gaza peace plan") as "realistic."[\[250\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Faiola_&_Craw_October_2025-261) Following the [Israeli strikes on Iran](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/June_2025_Israeli_strikes_on_Iran "June 2025 Israeli strikes on Iran") in June 2025, he urged Iranian and Israeli authorities to act with "reason".[\[251\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-262) On August 27, Leo said, "I beg for a permanent ceasefire to be reached, the safe entry of humanitarian aid to be facilitated and humanitarian law to be fully respected."[\[252\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-NBC,_Israel_faces_new_pressure_over_hospital_strikes,_August_27,_2025-263) [_The_ _Washington Post_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Washington_Post "The Washington Post") reported in September 2025 that Leo said the Vatican "at this time" cannot define the war as a "genocide", but he also noted that more and more people have described it as such.[\[253\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-264) Leo also issued prayers for those affected by the [clashes in southern Syria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_Syria_clashes_/(July_2025%E2%80%93present/) "Southern Syria clashes (July 2025–present)") and the [2025 Cambodia–Thailand clashes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Cambodia%E2%80%93Thailand_clashes "2025 Cambodia–Thailand clashes").[\[254\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-265) Leo lamented the [El Fasher massacre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/El_Fasher_massacre "El Fasher massacre") in [Sudan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sudan "Sudan") during his Sunday Angelus address on November 2, 2025, calling for a ceasefire and humanitarian aid.[\[255\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-266) In November 2025, Leo criticized the [United States' military strikes against alleged drug traffickers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_United_States_military_strikes_on_alleged_drug_traffickers "2025 United States military strikes on alleged drug traffickers") near [Venezuela](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venezuela "Venezuela"), warning that they were "increasing tension" and calling for diplomatic dialogue between the two countries.[\[256\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-AP_11-05-2025-267)

In his [Pentecost](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pentecost "Pentecost") homily soon after his election as Pope, Leo criticized the "exclusionary mindset" displayed by various [nationalist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nationalism "Nationalism") movements. The [Holy Spirit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holy_Spirit_in_Christianity "Holy Spirit in Christianity") "breaks down barriers and tears down the walls of indifference and hatred", he said.[\[257\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Reuters1-268) To Leo, areas advertised as "security zones" had the effect of "separating us from our neighbors" and spreading "prejudice". He proclaimed that the Church needed to "open the borders between peoples and break down the barriers between class and race."[\[257\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Reuters1-268) Leo additionally condemned [femicide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Femicide "Femicide") during the homily, calling it both painful and tragic and attributing it to "an unhealthy desire for domination."[\[258\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Korea_Herald_2025-269)[\[259\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Allen_2025-270)

#### US politics

Throughout his time as a bishop and as a cardinal, Prevost continued to vote in both state and federal elections in the United States, being a [registered voter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Voter_registration "Voter registration") in [Will County, Illinois](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Will_County,_Illinois "Will County, Illinois"). Illinois election law does not require voters to register affiliation with a political party, and Prevost has never officially done so.[\[260\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-271) The elections Prevost has voted in include the [2008 Democratic presidential primary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_Illinois_Democratic_presidential_primary "2008 Illinois Democratic presidential primary"), the Democratic primary for the [2010 Illinois gubernatorial election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_Illinois_gubernatorial_election#Democratic_primary "2010 Illinois gubernatorial election"), the [2012 Republican presidential primary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Illinois_Republican_presidential_primary "2012 Illinois Republican presidential primary"), the Republican primary for the [2014 Illinois gubernatorial election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Illinois_gubernatorial_election#Republican_primary "2014 Illinois gubernatorial election"), the [2016 Republican presidential primary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Illinois_Republican_presidential_primary "2016 Illinois Republican presidential primary"), and the [2024 United States general election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Illinois_elections "2024 Illinois elections").[\[261\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-272)[\[262\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-273)[\[263\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-274)

On the social media platform X (formerly [Twitter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twitter "Twitter")), Prevost's former account reposted posts critical of US immigration policies under President [Donald Trump](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Trump "Donald Trump") and Vice President [JD Vance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JD_Vance "JD Vance").[\[264\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-275) He has also expressed support for [COVID-19 vaccination](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_vaccination "COVID-19 vaccination") during the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic") and sympathy for [George Floyd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Floyd "George Floyd") and [protesters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Floyd_protests "George Floyd protests").[\[22\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-kim-25) His X account which he used prior to his election as Pope has since been deleted and he is currently using the official @Pontifex handle, inherited from Popes Benedict XVI and Francis.[\[265\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-276) As Pope, Leo avoided discussing US politics for the first few months of his pontificate, but in September 2025 reiterated past criticisms of the second Trump administration, remarking to a group of journalists that "someone who says 'I am against abortion but I am in agreement with the inhuman treatment of immigrants in the United States,' I don't know if that's pro-life."[\[266\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-McElwee_Trump_Leo_September_2025-277)[\[250\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Faiola_&_Craw_October_2025-261) White House press secretary [Karoline Leavitt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karoline_Leavitt "Karoline Leavitt") denied Leo's claims of maltreatment.[\[267\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Sentner_2025-278) That October, Leo urged labor unions in his home city of Chicago to fight for immigrants' rights. In November, he called for a "deep reflection" about American immigration policy and asked that detainees' "spiritual rights" be upheld via access to clergy.[\[256\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-AP_11-05-2025-267)

Personal life
-------------

In addition to his native English, Leo speaks Spanish, Italian, French, and Portuguese, as well as some German. He can also read Latin.[\[114\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-NCR_2025-121)[\[268\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-279)[\[269\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-280) During his time in Peru, Leo learned a little of one of the [Quechuan languages](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quechuan_languages "Quechuan languages").[\[270\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-281)[\[271\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-282) He has described himself as "quite the amateur tennis player".[\[272\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-283) He is the first Pope who writes his own emails and wears a smartwatch, specifically an [Apple Watch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apple_Watch "Apple Watch").[\[273\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Lamb-284) He regularly plays _[Wordle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wordle "Wordle")_ and _[Words with Friends](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Words_with_Friends "Words with Friends")_ with his brothers.[\[274\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-285)[\[275\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-286)

Leo is a lifelong fan of the [Chicago White Sox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_White_Sox "Chicago White Sox") of [Major League Baseball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_League_Baseball "Major League Baseball"),[\[276\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-287)[\[277\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-288)[\[278\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-289) and was in attendance at [US Cellular Field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/US_Cellular_Field "US Cellular Field") for Game 1 of the [2005 World Series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_World_Series "2005 World Series").[\[279\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-290)[\[280\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-291)[\[281\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-292) His support for [Chicago sports](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sports_in_Chicago "Sports in Chicago") also extends to the [National Football League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Football_League "National Football League")'s [Chicago Bears](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Bears "Chicago Bears"); United States Vice President [JD Vance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JD_Vance "JD Vance") presented him with a custom Bears jersey following his papal inauguration, which Leo remarked was a "good choice".[\[282\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-293) He has also shown support for [Villanova University athletics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Villanova_University_athletics "Villanova University athletics"), especially the [Villanova Wildcats men's basketball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Villanova_Wildcats_men%27s_basketball "Villanova Wildcats men's basketball") team.[\[283\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-294) In a review of an upcoming biography about him, the _Washington Post_ reported that in a hypothetical [World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIFA_World_Cup "FIFA World Cup") match-up between the [United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_men%27s_national_soccer_team "United States men's national soccer team") and [Peru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peru_national_football_team "Peru national football team"), Leo would support Peru.[\[284\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-295)

As a teenager, he enjoyed driving recreationally.[\[40\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Tucker_2025-44) Throughout his life, he has frequently preferred [driving long distances](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Road_trip "Road trip") for journeys where most people would prefer to fly, such as from Philadelphia to Chicago, Brisbane to Sydney, and Chiclayo to Lima.[\[9\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Horowitz,_Bosman,_Dias,_Graham,_Romero_&_Taj_2025-12) He also repaired cars himself as a bishop in Chiclayo.[\[285\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-296)

For two years before becoming pope, Prevost, aged 68–69, would go two to three times a week to a gym for an hour, with a workout plan designed for men aged 50–55, focusing on posture and cardiovascular health. His personal trainer recalled Prevost's stamina and his being "always positive about everything".[\[286\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-297)

During his time as bishop of Chiclayo, aside from daily [Mass](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eucharist "Eucharist") celebrated at 8 p.m. to ensure a clear mind, Prevost had [periods of prayer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mental_prayer "Mental prayer") at the beginning of the day and before dinner. He prayed [lauds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lauds "Lauds") in the morning at the Cathedral and the [rosary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosary "Rosary") with his priest colleagues around noon.[\[86\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Beltr%C3%A1n-91)

Honors
------

Villanova awarded him an honorary [Doctor of Humanities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_of_Humanities "Doctor of Humanities") degree in 2014.[\[49\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Mervosh_2025-53) In 2025, _[Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_/(magazine/) "Time (magazine)")_ magazine included Leo among [the world's 100 most influential people](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_100 "Time 100") in [Artificial Intelligence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artificial_Intelligence "Artificial Intelligence").[\[287\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-298) On October 23, 2025, King [Charles III](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_III "Charles III") appointed Leo an Honorary Knight Grand Cross of the [Order of the Bath](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Order_of_the_Bath "Order of the Bath") on the occasion of the King's [state visit to the Holy See](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_visit_by_Charles_III_to_the_Holy_See "State visit by Charles III to the Holy See").[\[288\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-299) At the same event Leo accepted the title of _Papal Confrater of St. George's Chapel_ in Windsor Castle.[\[289\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-300)

2.  **[^](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_ref-5)** Pronounced [_PREE\-vohst_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Pronunciation_respelling_key "Help:Pronunciation respelling key").[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-3) The surname, of [Northwest Italian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northwest_Italy "Northwest Italy") origin, is derived from the [Piedmontese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piedmontese_language "Piedmontese language") or [Lombard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lombard_language "Lombard language") _prevòst_, customarily meaning 'parish priest', cognate with the English _[provost](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Provost_/(religion/) "Provost (religion)")_, from the Latin _praepositus_.[\[3\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Serra_2025-4)
3.  **[^](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_ref-10)** While working in Peru and Latin America as bishop (2015–2023), Prevost customarily used the name "Robert Francis Prevost Martínez" in accordance with [Hispanic naming customs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_naming_customs "Spanish naming customs"), as Martínez is his mother's family name.[\[4\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-6)[\[5\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-7)[\[6\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-8)[\[7\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-9)
4.  **[^](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_ref-42)** St. Mary's Church in Dolton was closed in 2011.[\[38\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-41)
5.  **[^](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_ref-80)** That Ray was allowed to live at the friary was first reported by the _[Chicago Sun-Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Sun-Times "Chicago Sun-Times")_ in 2021, based on documents the church made public in 2014.[\[75\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Herguth_2021-79)
6.  **[^](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_ref-95)** His role in Callao ended upon the installation of a new bishop there on May 26, 2021.
7.  **[^](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_ref-112)** This interview was conducted while Prevost was bishop but was published after he was elected pope.[\[105\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-AFP_2025-111)
8.  **[^](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_ref-124)** Francis appointed him to the [Dicastery for Evangelization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dicastery_for_Evangelization "Dicastery for Evangelization") (Section for First Evangelization and New Particular Churches), [Dicastery for the Doctrine of the Faith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dicastery_for_the_Doctrine_of_the_Faith "Dicastery for the Doctrine of the Faith"), [Dicastery for the Eastern Churches](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dicastery_for_the_Eastern_Churches "Dicastery for the Eastern Churches"), [Dicastery for the Clergy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dicastery_for_the_Clergy "Dicastery for the Clergy"), [Dicastery for Institutes of Consecrated Life and Societies of Apostolic Life](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dicastery_for_Institutes_of_Consecrated_Life_and_Societies_of_Apostolic_Life "Dicastery for Institutes of Consecrated Life and Societies of Apostolic Life"), [Dicastery for Culture and Education](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dicastery_for_Culture_and_Education "Dicastery for Culture and Education"), and [Dicastery for Legislative Texts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dicastery_for_Legislative_Texts "Dicastery for Legislative Texts").[\[12\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Vatican_News_2025-15)
9.  **[^](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_ref-128)** Prevost's plan to take possession of Albano on May 12 were cancelled when the conclave to elect Francis' successor was scheduled.[\[119\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-127)
10.  **[^](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_ref-156)** He is the 265th person to become Pope as [Pope Benedict IX](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Benedict_IX "Pope Benedict IX") was elected three times.
11.  **[^](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_ref-237)** The positions of cardinals are difficult to pinpoint in political terms and different labels, more specific to the Church's context like _sinodali_ (supporters of synodality), _lealisti_ (loyalists, the supporters of the reigning pope), and _tradizionalisti_ (traditionalists), are applied. Nonetheless, Prevost was generally seen as a "reformer of the Bergoglian area", not far from other more progressive names like [Pietro Parolin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pietro_Parolin "Pietro Parolin") and [Luis Antonio Tagle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Antonio_Tagle "Luis Antonio Tagle"), and more moderate than others like [Robert Walter McElroy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Walter_McElroy "Robert Walter McElroy") and [Matteo Maria Zuppi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matteo_Maria_Zuppi "Matteo Maria Zuppi").[\[226\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-236)

### Honoring our Augustinian brother, Pope Leo XIV

HABEMUS PAPAM
-------------

**Official Statement from the Midwest Augustinian Province of Our Mother of Good Counsel on the Election of Pope Leo XIV**
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

**CHICAGO, IL. (May 8, 2025)**

The Midwest Augustinian Province of Our Mother of Good Counsel rejoices in the historic election of our brother, Cardinal Robert Francis Prevost, O.S.A., as the 267th pope of the Roman Catholic Church, taking the name Pope Leo XIV. His election marks a moment of profound significance—not only as the first pope from the United States, but also as the first Augustinian to be elected pontiff.

“Pope Leo XIV is a man of deep integrity, a true listener, and a companion to those on the margins of society,” said Prior Provincial Very Rev. Anthony B. Pizzo, O.S.A. “We see him as a bridge-builder, rooted in the spirit of St. Augustine, walking forward with the whole Church as a companion on the journey. We are honored that he is one of our own, a brother formed in the restless heart of the Augustinian Order.”

Born in Chicago in 1955, Pope Leo XIV entered our novitiate in 1977 and made his solemn profession in 1981. Following priestly ordination in 1982, he went on to earn advanced degrees in canon law in Rome and spent the next decades serving the Church with humility and distinction—as a missionary in Peru, as an educator and formator, as Prior Provincial of our own Province, and later as Prior General of the entire Augustinian Order for two terms.

After returning to the Province in 2013, he was called once more to missionary service, this time as Apostolic Administrator and then Bishop of Chiclayo, Peru. His episcopal ministry was marked by a pastoral heart, dedication to formation, and care for the poor. His leadership in the Church continued to expand: as a member of the Congregation for the Clergy, the Congregation for Bishops, Apostolic Administrator of Callao, and ultimately, as Prefect of the Dicastery for Bishops and President of the Pontifical Commission for Latin America. In 2023, he was created Cardinal by Pope Francis and, in 2025, elevated to the Order of Bishops within the College of Cardinals.

Now, in divine providence and guided by the Holy Spirit, our brother has been entrusted with the Chair of Peter.

Pope Leo XIV brings to the papacy the heart of an Augustinian: a love for community, a thirst for truth, and a shepherd’s care for the people of God. His life of mission, teaching, and servant leadership reflect the best of our tradition.

We offer him our prayers, our love, and our unwavering support. May his pontificate be a source of unity, peace, and renewal for the Church and the world.

In Augustine,

**The Midwest Augustinian Province of Our Mother of Good Counsel**

**_Mission Statement:_**

_We, the Augustinians of the Province of Our Mother of Good Counsel, are members of the worldwide Order of Saint  Augustine in the Roman Catholic Church. Centered in the Eucharist and prayer, we search for God in community by sharing our lives, goods and spiritual journey with each other and the people of God. In harmony of mind and heart on our journey toward God, our experience of common life flows into and shapes our ministries. We continue to serve the Church in schools, parishes and missions as we seek to discern new paths of service to which God calls us._

Augustinian Biography of Robert F. Prevost, O.S.A.
--------------------------------------------------

Robert Francis Prevost was born on September 14, 1955, in Chicago, Illinois, to Louis M. and Mildred A. Prevost.

He studied for four years at St. Augustine High School Seminary in Holland, Michigan, where he earned his diploma in 1973. He continued in the Pre-Novitiate formation program at Villanova University in Villanova, Pennsylvania, earning a B.S. in Mathematics in 1977.

Robert was received into the Augustinian Novitiate on September 1, 1977. He professed temporary vows in the Order of St. Augustine on September 2, 1978.  He completed theological studies at Catholic Theological Union in Chicago and earned a Master’s of Divinity Degree in 1981. He professed solemn vows on August 29, 1981, and was ordained a priest on June 19, 1982.  From 1981 to 1985, he studied Canon Law at the Pontifical University of St. Thomas Aquinas (Angelicum) in Rome. He earned a Licentiate in 1984 and a Doctorate in 1987.

Father Prevost was named Chancellor of the Diocese of Chulucanas, Peru, in 1985. He returned to the United States in 1986 and served as Vocations Director for the Province of Our Mother of Good Counsel until 1988. He also was temporary Director of the Province Mission Office during this time.

In 1988, Father Prevost returned to Trujillo, Peru, to initiate the first common formation house between the Vicariates of Chulucanas, Iquitos, and Apurimac. In this community, in service to the pre-novices and the professed, he occupied the posts of Prior (1988-1992), Formation Director (1988-1999), Master of Professed (1993-1998), and parish priest of the Parish of Saint Mary of Monserrat. In the Archdiocese of Trujillo, he served as the Prefect of Studies at the Archdiocesan Seminary of San Carlos and San Marcelo, and he also taught Canon Law there.  During this time, he also served as Judge of the Regional Ecclesiastical Tribunal and as a member of the College of Consultors in Trujillo.

He was elected Prior Provincial of the Province of Our Mother of Good Counsel in 1998 and returned to the United States to begin this role in 1999.

At the Ordinary General Chapter of 2001, Father Prevost was elected Prior General of the worldwide Augustinian Order. He was elected to a second term at the Ordinary General Chapter of 2007 and served until his term ended in September 2013.

Following his time as Prior General, Father Prevost returned to the Province of Our Mother of Good Counsel and served in several roles: Director of Formation at St. Augustine Friary, Vicar Provincial, First Counselor, Board Member of Villanova University, and Board Member of Catholic Theological Union.

On November 4, 2014, it was announced that Pope Francis had appointed Father Prevost as Apostolic Administrator of the Diocese of Chiclayo, Peru, and Titular Bishop of Sufar.  He was installed as Apostolic Administrator of Chiclayo on November 7, 2014, and was ordained Titular Bishop of Sufar on December 12, 2014.  He was installed as Bishop of Chiclayo on September 26, 2015.

Within the Episcopal Conference of Peru, he served on the permanent council from 2018-2020.  He was elected in 2019 as President for the Commission on Education and Culture. He was also a member of the leadership of Caritas Peru.

On July 13, 2019, Bishop Prevost was appointed to the Vatican’s Congregation for the Clergy.  From April 15, 2020, until May 26, 2021, he served as Apostolic Administrator of the Diocese of Callao, Peru. On November 21, 2020, he was appointed to the Vatican’s Congregation for Bishops.

On January 30, 2023, Pope Francis appointed Bishop Prevost as Prefect of the Dicastery for Bishops (formerly Congregation of Bishops) with the title Archbishop-Bishop Emeritus of Chiclayo.  He was also appointed the President of the Pontifical Commission of Latin America.  He began both of these roles on April 12, 2023.

It was announced on July 9, 2023, that Pope Francis would elevate Archbishop Prevost to be a Cardinal at the Vatican consistory on Sept. 30, 2023.  At the ceremony, he gave a speech on behalf of the other cardinals-elect.  He continues to serve as Prefect of the Dicastery for Bishops and as President of the Pontifical Commission of Latin America.  He is also a member of several other Dicasteries.

On February 6, 2025, he was elevated from Cardinal-Deacon to Cardinal-Bishop within the College of Cardinals. He was assigned the title of the Suburbicarian Church of Albano.

On May 8, 2025, he was elected Pope and chose the name Pope Leo XIV.

Top Questions

### 

What did Leo XIV do before becoming pope in 2025?

### 

What is Leo XIV’s educational background?

News •
------

**Leo XIV** (born September 14, 1955, Chicago, [Illinois](https://www.britannica.com/place/Illinois-state), U.S.) is the [pope](https://www.britannica.com/topic/pope), the leader of the [Roman Catholic Church](https://www.britannica.com/topic/Roman-Catholicism). He was elected to the [papacy](https://www.britannica.com/topic/papacy) on May 8, 2025, succeeding Pope [Francis](https://www.britannica.com/biography/Francis-I-pope) and becoming the first American pope in history. An [Augustinian](https://www.britannica.com/topic/Augustinians) [priest](https://www.britannica.com/topic/priest-Christianity) who performed [extensive](https://www.britannica.com/dictionary/extensive) missionary work in [Peru](https://www.britannica.com/place/Peru) and served as head of the Augustinian order from 2001 to 2013, he was made a [cardinal](https://www.britannica.com/topic/cardinal-Roman-Catholicism) by Francis in 2023. He brings a reputation for being a fair, deft administrator and a political moderate, and he is expected to continue his predecessor’s agenda for the church.

Leo’s vision for the church
---------------------------

Words of a Future Pope

“The lack of unity is a wound that the church suffers, a very painful one. Divisions and polemics in the church do not help anything. We bishops especially must accelerate this movement toward unity, toward communion in the church.” —Bishop Robert Prevost to [_Vatican News_](https://www.vaticannews.va/en/vatican-city/news/2023-05/archbishop-prevost-the-bishop-is-a-pastor-not-a-manager.html), May 2023

In his first address as pope, Leo XIV told the crowd assembled in St. Peter’s Square in [Vatican City](https://www.britannica.com/place/Vatican-City), “I am a son of [St. Augustine](https://www.britannica.com/biography/Saint-Augustine), an Augustinian. He said, ‘With you I am a [Christian](https://www.britannica.com/topic/Christianity), for you a [bishop](https://www.britannica.com/topic/bishop-Christianity).’ So may we all walk together towards that homeland that God has prepared for us.”

Notably, the last pope to choose Leo as a papal name, [Leo XIII](https://www.britannica.com/biography/Leo-XIII) (reigned 1878–1903), was known for his conciliatory approach to civil governments, for his concern toward renewing a [dialogue](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/dialogue) between the church and the modern world, and for authoring [_Rerum novarum_](https://www.britannica.com/topic/Rerum-Novarum) (1891; “Of New Things), a landmark papal [encyclical](https://www.britannica.com/topic/encyclical) that addressed the economic and social problems created by the [Industrial Revolution](https://www.britannica.com/event/Industrial-Revolution) and laid down the [principles of Catholic social teaching](https://www.britannica.com/topic/Rerum-Novarum). For Catholics worldwide, the new pope’s choice of a name and his professional history signified that he planned to bring a similar diplomatic and unifying spirit to church divisions and a pastoral approach to issues of [social justice](https://www.britannica.com/topic/social-justice).

[(_Read about why the name a pope chooses matters._)](https://www.britannica.com/topic/Why-the-Name-a-Pope-Chooses-Matters)

Indeed, two days after the [conclave](https://www.britannica.com/topic/papal-conclave) that elected him, Leo [explained his choice of name](https://www.vatican.va/content/leo-xiv/en/speeches/2025/may/documents/20250510-collegio-cardinalizio.html) to the [College of Cardinals](https://www.britannica.com/topic/Sacred-College-of-Cardinals), noting the historic message of _Rerum novarum_ and its relevance in the age of [artificial intelligence](https://www.britannica.com/technology/artificial-intelligence). In that address, Leo also asked the cardinals to renew their commitment to the principles of the [Second Vatican Council](https://www.britannica.com/event/Second-Vatican-Council) (1962–65), which introduced sweeping modernizing changes in the church, and to Pope Francis’s 2013 document _Evangelii gaudium_ (“The Joy of the Gospel”), which [envisions](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/envisions) a church that embraces its global [diversity](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/diversity) and champions the poor.

[Childhood home of Pope Leo XIV](https://cdn.britannica.com/97/279297-050-1EEACA8F/Childhood-home-of-Pope-Leo-XIV.jpg)The modest childhood home of Pope Leo XIV (born Robert Prevost in 1955) in Dolton, a suburb of the South Side of Chicago.

Hailing from the far South Side of [Chicago](https://www.britannica.com/place/Chicago), Prevost was one of three children born to Louis and Mildred (Martínez) Prevost, a school principal and a librarian, respectively. Like many Americans, Prevost comes from a background that reflects the diversity of both the United States and the Catholic Church. His [family’s roots](https://www.nytimes.com/interactive/2025/06/11/magazine/pope-leo-xiv-ancestry-family-tree.html) include Spanish, Cuban, Italian, French Canadian, and African American ([Creole](https://www.britannica.com/topic/Creole)) ancestry. His maternal grandparents, who migrated to Chicago from [Louisiana](https://www.britannica.com/place/Louisiana-state), were described in historical records as Black or “[mulatto](https://www.britannica.com/topic/mulatto-people).”

In Chicago, Prevost [attended](https://www.britannica.com/dictionary/attended) a local Catholic elementary school and served as an altar boy, then entered St. Augustine Seminary High School in [Holland](https://www.britannica.com/place/Holland-Michigan), [Michigan](https://www.britannica.com/place/Michigan), graduating in 1973. From there he enrolled in [Villanova University](https://www.britannica.com/topic/Villanova-University) near [Philadelphia](https://www.britannica.com/place/Philadelphia), earning a B.A. in mathematics in 1977. That same year he began his novitiate in the Augustinian order and took his solemn [vows](https://www.britannica.com/topic/vow) four years later. He was [ordained](https://www.britannica.com/topic/ordination) a priest in 1982.

Prevost studied at Catholic Theological Union in Chicago and received a master’s in divinity in 1982. He then headed to [Rome](https://www.britannica.com/place/Rome) to study [canon law](https://www.britannica.com/topic/canon-law) at the Pontifical University of St. Thomas Aquinas. He earned a license in canon law in 1984. His doctoral thesis (1987) was on the role of the local prior in the Augustinian order.

Missionary work in Peru and career in Chicago
---------------------------------------------

Much of Prevost’s career was spent between Peru and Chicago. In 1985 he began missionary work with the Augustinians in Peru, and he was quickly made chancellor (1985–86) of the territorial prelature in Chulucanas. From 1987 to 1988 he served as director of vocations and [missions](https://www.britannica.com/topic/missions-Christianity) of the Midwest Augustinian Province of Our Mother of Good [Counsel](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/Counsel) in Chicago. Beginning in 1988 he would spend the next decade in Peru as director of an Augustinian seminary in [Trujillo](https://www.britannica.com/place/Trujillo-Peru). He took on many roles there, including teaching canon law and serving as a [parish](https://www.britannica.com/topic/parish-religion) priest, prefect of the diocesan seminary in Trujillo, and judicial [vicar](https://www.britannica.com/topic/vicar) of the Trujillo archdiocese.

In 1999 Prevost returned to Chicago to serve as prior of Our Mother of Good Counsel. His [tenure](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/tenure) in this role later proved controversial after he allegedly signed off on a decision to allow a priest who had been accused of [sexually abusing](https://www.britannica.com/topic/sexual-abuse) minors to live in a [monastery](https://www.britannica.com/topic/monastery) close to a school. His defenders would later say that he was following the U.S. church’s [protocol](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/protocol), which had yet to adopt new standards regarding [clergy abuse](https://www.britannica.com/topic/Catholic-Church-Sexual-Abuse-Crisis) accusations.

Head of the Augustinians and tenure as bishop and cardinal
----------------------------------------------------------

Prevost was elected prior general of the entire Augustinian order in 2001, which required him to live in Rome. Serving two terms in this role, he earned a reputation as an effective administrator.

[Cathedral of Saint Mary in Chiclayo](https://cdn.britannica.com/06/273106-050-1B255A14/Catedral-de-Santa-maria-Cathedral-of-Saint-Mary-Chiclayo-Peru-Pope-Leo-XIV-celebrated-mass.jpg)The Cathedral of Saint Mary (Catedral de Santa María) in Chiclayo, Peru. Before becoming Pope Leo XIV in 2025, Robert Prevost served as bishop of the diocese of Chiclayo beginning in 2015.

In 2014 Francis appointed Prevost apostolic administrator of the diocese of [Chiclayo](https://www.britannica.com/place/Chiclayo) in Peru, and the following year Prevost was made [bishop](https://www.britannica.com/topic/bishop-Christianity) of the diocese. He also served as second vice president and as a council member of the Peruvian Episcopal Conference from 2018 to 2023. Prevost’s time in Peru at this stage received [criticism](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/criticism) for what some groups claimed was his mishandling of [sexual abuse](https://www.britannica.com/topic/sexual-abuse) allegations against two priests. The diocese, however, maintains that he followed correct procedures and that the accusations were investigated. At the same time, he and other Peruvian bishops were seen as a stabilizing force during political upheavals and disagreements between proponents of [liberation theology](https://www.britannica.com/topic/liberation-theology) and the [conservative](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/conservative) Peruvian-based religious group Sodalitium Christianae Vitae (SCV; Sodality of Christian Life). Indeed, the Peruvian Episcopal Conference noted that Prevost played a crucial role in a [truth commission](https://www.britannica.com/topic/truth-commission) that exposed [corruption](https://www.britannica.com/topic/corruption-law) and abuse in the SCV, which was officially dissolved by Pope Francis in April 2025.

After Prevost was elected pope, further questions arose about the legitimacy of the two abuse accusations in Peru. In 2025 one of the [alleged](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/alleged) victims publicly stated that she was not sure of the motives of the lawyer who had pursued the case and who had ties to the SCV.

In January 2023 Prevost was appointed prefect of the [Roman Curia](https://www.britannica.com/topic/Roman-Curia)’s Dicastery for Bishops, a powerful role that put him in charge of selecting bishops around the world. He was also appointed president of the Pontifical Commission for [Latin America](https://www.britannica.com/place/Latin-America). Later that year he was made a [cardinal](https://www.britannica.com/topic/cardinal-Roman-Catholicism) by Francis.

First American pope
-------------------

[2025 Jubilee of Youth](https://cdn.britannica.com/36/275936-050-87BF523F/Pope-Leo-XIV-arrives-to-Jubilee-of-Youth-August-2025.jpg)Pope Leo XIV arriving by helicopter to Tor Vergata, on the outskirts of Rome, for the Jubilee of Youth prayer vigil on August 2, 2025. Half a million young Catholics attended the 2025 Jubilee of Youth, which coincided with the international celebration of World Youth Day.

A citizen of both the [United States](https://www.britannica.com/place/United-States) and Peru (naturalized in 2015), Leo is the second pope to come from the [Western Hemisphere](https://www.britannica.com/place/Western-Hemisphere) (his predecessor, Pope Francis of [Argentina](https://www.britannica.com/place/Argentina), was the first). Leo’s election as the first pope from the United States is especially historic because it breaks from the traditional view that a papal candidate should not be selected from a global superpower. However, some observers have noted that his dual citizenship and experience working with the poor in Peru could [assuage](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/assuage) concerns of the United States influencing church governance. (Notably, in 1899 it was another Pope [Leo](https://www.britannica.com/biography/Leo-XIII) who condemned [Americanism](https://www.britannica.com/topic/Americanism), a movement that attempted to [reconcile](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/reconcile) Catholicism and American culture.) Meanwhile, in his hometown of Chicago, many locals expressed more concern about whether the new pope preferred the [Cubs](https://www.britannica.com/topic/Chicago-Cubs) or the [White Sox](https://www.britannica.com/topic/Chicago-White-Sox), the city’s rival [baseball](https://www.britannica.com/sports/baseball) teams. (It was later confirmed that he supports the Sox.)

[(_Why hasn’t there been an American pope?_)](https://www.britannica.com/topic/Why-Hasnt-There-Been-an-American-Pope)

Stance on social issues
-----------------------

“I don’t think he’ll be the silent one.”—John Prevost on his brother Pope Leo XIV’s views, [May 2025](https://www.nytimes.com/live/2025/05/08/world/pope-conclave-news#pope-leo-xiv-brother-john-prevost)

Prevost’s election to the papacy in May 2025 was seen by some as a compromise between more liberal and conservative [contenders](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/contenders). Although he has been less vocal than many other bishops and cardinals in sharing his views, he has expressed strong support of several of Francis’s programs, especially on the issues of protecting the [environment](https://www.britannica.com/science/environment) and the rights of migrants. Immediately after Leo’s election, his brother John Prevost [told _The New York Times_](https://www.britannica.com/), “I know he’s not happy with what’s going on with immigration \[in the United States\]. I know that for a fact. How far he’ll go with it is only one’s guess, but he won’t just sit back. I don’t think he’ll be the silent one.”

Indeed, before he was elected pope, Leo posted on [social media](https://www.britannica.com/topic/social-media) his criticism of U.S. Vice Pres. [J.D. Vance](https://www.britannica.com/biography/J-D-Vance)’s views on Christian [doctrine](https://www.britannica.com/topic/doctrine) regarding immigration. Earlier in 2025 Vance justified the deportation of immigrants by saying that St. Augustine’s [concept](https://www.britannica.com/dictionary/concept) of _ordo amoris_ (order of love) puts love of [country](https://www.britannica.com/topic/nation-state) and family ahead of love of one’s neighbors. Prevost posted that this interpretation was wrong.

On other issues, such as the blessing of [same-sex marriages](https://www.britannica.com/topic/same-sex-marriage) or ordaining women as [deacons](https://www.britannica.com/topic/deacon), the new pope has been more reserved in expressing his support. In a [September 2025 interview with _Crux_ magazine](https://cruxnow.com/vatican/2025/09/pope-leo-speaks-to-cruxs-elise-ann-allen-about-lgbtq-issues-and-the-liturgy), Leo said that while he plans to appoint women to church leadership roles, he does not intend to change church teaching on the issue of ordaining women, noting that there are more pressing concerns to address regarding clericalism and the diaconate. On the subject of [LGBTQ+](https://www.britannica.com/topic/LGTBQ-community) Catholics and their place in the church, Leo called the issue a [polarizing](https://www.britannica.com/dictionary/polarizing) one but added, “Everyone’s invited in, but I don’t invite a person in because they are or are not of any specific identity. I invite a person in because they are a son or daughter of God.” Asserting that “individuals will be accepted and received” by the church, he told _Crux_ that church doctrine on the matter is unlikely to change in the near future.

Quick Facts

Original name:

Robert Francis Prevost

The following month Leo published his first apostolic exhortation, [_Dilexit te_](https://www.vatican.va/content/leo-xiv/en/apost_exhortations/documents/20251004-dilexi-te.html) (“I Have Loved You”), which was begun by Francis and addresses the church’s obligation to care for the poor.

[René Ostberg](https://www.britannica.com/editor/rene-ostberg/12853185)

Leo XIV Is the Pope. Apparently, No One Told AI.
================================================

ChatGPT is not the only AI chatbot that seems to have a Pope Leo-shaped blind spot.

    ![Image 5: Pope Leo XIV greets the faithful from his popemobile after Mass and proclamation of Saint John Henry Newman as 'Doctor of the Church.'](https://publisher-ncreg.s3.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/pb-ncregister/swp/hv9hms/media/20251103101140_0fc72e0494451c7168656f1794984ac03e03d245f1e55d1a2797771c917219ec.jpg)

Pope Leo XIV greets the faithful from his popemobile after Mass and proclamation of Saint John Henry Newman as 'Doctor of the Church.' (photo: Daniel Ibanez / EWTN News )

[Jonah McKeown](https://www.ncregister.com/author/jonah-mckeown) [Nation](https://www.ncregister.com/section/nation) November 3, 2025

For months now, something odd has happened when [some internet users](https://www.reddit.com/r/CatholicMemes/comments/1kvae8w/chatgpt_doesnt_know_about_pope_leo_and_is/) — including me — ask [ChatGPT](https://chatgpt.com/), the ubiquitous artificial intelligence tool from OpenAI, about Pope Leo XIV.

“It looks like there might be a bit of confusion with the name, as there has never been a Pope Leo XIV. However, there have been several popes named Leo in history,” the chatbot replied to a query made Oct. 31.

Not all ChatGPT users are experiencing this phenomenon — if you go to ChatGPT right now and ask, “Who is the pope?” it may well give you the correct answer. To put it mildly, though, it’s hit or miss.

Another user (and fellow EWTN employee), who was recently seeking information about Opus Dei, tried to correct ChatGPT when it referred to Pope Francis as if he were the current pontiff. “The current pope is Leo XIV,” the user wrote.

“Pope Leo XIV does not exist,” the chatbot insisted.

“As of right now (October 2025), the pope is still Pope Francis (Jorge Mario Bergoglio), elected in 2013. There has been no resignation, conclave, or papal death since then — which would be required for there to be a new pope.”

But that wasn’t all. The program doubled down and adopted what some might perceive as a rather patronizing tone:

“If someone told you ‘Leo XIV,’ they are either: joking/using a fictional or speculative scenario, confusing a rumor or prophecy, or genuinely misinformed,” it said.

But the experience of another fellow EWTN employee took the cake. It appears that ChatGPT can notice the existence of Pope Leo — but has a hard time letting his predecessor go.

“People are saying that you are saying Pope Francis isn’t dead,” that user typed out to ChatGPT.

“Pope Francis is alive, but he resigned from the papacy earlier this year due to health reasons,” the chatbot confidently — and erroneously — began.

“After his resignation, the College of Cardinals elected Pope Leo XIV (Robert Francis Prevost) as his successor on May 8, 2025. Francis has reportedly been living quietly in the Vatican’s Mater Ecclesiae Monastery, occasionally appearing at Vatican ceremonies.” (It shouldn’t even need to be said, but … none of that is true, apart from the election of Pope Leo.)

And ChatGPT is not the only AI chatbot that seems to have a Pope Leo-shaped blind spot. [Claude,](https://claude.ai/login?returnTo=%2F%3F) an AI assistant made by Anthropic, and [DeepSeek](https://www.deepseek.com/), a much-hyped Chinese product, both denied the existence of Pope Leo XIV in response to queries made Oct. 31. In contrast, Google’s [Gemini](https://www.google.com/url?sa=t&source=web&rct=j&opi=89978449&url=https://gemini.google.com/&ved=2ahUKEwjjv62cpM-QAxXg48kDHYHGGFkQFnoECA0QAQ&usg=AOvVaw0NAGHCxxuvW-RqAT62pGZI) and the AI search engine [Perplexity](https://www.perplexity.ai/) both knew who Pope Leo was and immediately returned information on him.

So, what’s going on? It all has to do with the way AI models are trained and how they operate in practice.

AI chatbots rely on large language models (LLMs), which are “trained” by ingesting massive amounts of data. The models in use today can only be trained up to a certain date, which differs depending on the chatbot.

Paid users of ChatGPT are using the “next generation” model, [GPT-5](https://openai.com/index/introducing-gpt-5/), which was launched on Aug. 7, 2025. Because it was released after the election of Pope Leo XIV, GPT-5 users can rest assured that that model “knows” about his existence.

But for those using ChatGPT’s previous model, GPT-4, its knowledge base cuts off in June 2024. For DeepSeek, the cutoff was “early 2024.” For Claude, it’s January 2025.

That doesn’t mean these chatbots with holes in their knowledge bases can’t search for and reference current information from the internet, however. In fact, ChatGPT, though it appears to lack information about Pope Leo in its GPT-4 knowledge base, can be prompted to do this.

After I specifically asked it to look up information on Pope Leo online, the chatbot finally conceded … _Habemus papam_ (“We have a pope”). “So why did you tell me earlier that he doesn’t exist?” I then wondered.

“That’s a great question — and you’re absolutely right to ask,” the chatbot began genially.

“When I first answered, I was relying on my built-in knowledge base, which only goes up to June 2024. At that point, Pope Francis was still pope, and Pope Leo XIV had not yet been elected. When you asked me to check again, I used live web search, which confirmed that Cardinal Robert Francis Prevost was elected pope in May 2025, taking the name Leo XIV — the first American pope in history. So, the difference comes down to timing.”

So … sedevacantist conspiracy in Silicon Valley? Almost certainly not. It’s clear that the election of the first American pope took everyone by surprise — even the robots.

Here is a link to watch the documentary. Article explaining the production is below.

On June 20, 2025, the Vatican media will release a new documentary titled _[León de Perú,](https://www.vaticannews.va/es/papa/news/2025-06/proximo-estreno-de-documental-leon-de-peru.html)_ spotlighting the missionary years of [Pope Leo XIV](https://aleteia.org/2025/05/08/pope-leo-xiv-a-name-steeped-in-history-and-hope/) — formerly Robert Francis Prevost — in Peru. Arriving just over six weeks after the start of his pontificate, the film offers a timely insight into **the pastoral and social journey that shaped the future pope**.

The documentary retraces Prevost’s footsteps through various Peruvian cities, including Chulucanas, Trujillo, Lima, Callao, and Chiclayo.

Prevost joined the Augustinian mission in Peru in 1985, three years after his ordination. He was back in Illinois for a year in 1987, and then back to Peru in 1988. He led the Augustinian seminary there and in 2014, was named the apostolic administrator of Chiclayo. He continued to serve as a Peruvian bishop until Pope Francis called him to the Vatican at the beginning of 2023.

Viewers will hear from numerous witnesses who recount his deep involvement in community life and his enduring commitment to the people he served. Their testimonies, woven into the film, paint a vivid portrait of a man marked by compassion, humility, and a tireless sense of mission.

Produced by the Editorial Direction of the [Vatican’s Dicastery for Communication](https://www.comunicazione.va/en.html), _León de Perú_ is a collaboration between journalists Salvatore Cernuzio, Felipe Herrera-Espaliat, and Jaime Vizcaíno Haro.

The film will be released at 5:00 p.m. Rome time across Vatican media platforms in Spanish, English, and Italian, including the Vatican News YouTube channel.

An advance screening will take place at 4:00 p.m. in the [Vatican Filmoteca](https://www.comunicazione.va/en/filmoteca-vaticana.html) for accredited journalists, offering a first look at the documentary’s narrative and its portrayal of Pope Leo XIV’s formative years.

The Vatican’s move to produce this documentary so early in Pope Leo’s pontificate signals **a desire to deepen public understanding of his roots** — not only as a Church leader but as a servant of the people. In a time when the Church is called to renew its closeness to the marginalized and forgotten, _León de Perú_ reminds audiences of the transformative power of mission lived with authenticity.
