15.content:
[](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Pope_Leo_XIV&action=edit&section=0&oldformat=true)**Pope Leo XIV**[\[a\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-2) (born **Robert Francis Prevost**,[\[b\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-5)[\[c\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-10) September 14, 1955) is the head of the [Catholic Church](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Catholic_Church "Catholic Church") and sovereign of [Vatican City](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Vatican_City "Vatican City"). He is the first Pope to have been born in the [United States](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/United_States "United States"), the first to hold either [U.S.](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Citizenship_of_the_United_States "Citizenship of the United States") or [Peruvian citizenships](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Peruvian_nationality_law "Peruvian nationality law"), the first from the [Order of Saint Augustine](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Order_of_Saint_Augustine "Order of Saint Augustine"), and the second (after his immediate predecessor [Pope Francis](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Francis "Pope Francis")) from the [Americas](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Americas "Americas").

**Quick facts** Pope Leo XIV, Church ...

Prevost was born in [Chicago](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Chicago "Chicago") and raised in the nearby suburb of [Dolton, Illinois](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Dolton,_Illinois "Dolton, Illinois"). He became a [friar](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Friar "Friar") in the Order of Saint Augustine in 1977 and was ordained as a priest in 1982. He earned a [Doctor of Canon Law](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Doctor_of_Canon_Law_/(Catholic_Church/) "Doctor of Canon Law (Catholic Church)") (JCD) degree in 1987 from the [Pontifical University of Saint Thomas Aquinas](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pontifical_University_of_Saint_Thomas_Aquinas "Pontifical University of Saint Thomas Aquinas") in [Rome](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Rome "Rome"). His service includes extensive [missionary](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Missionary "Missionary") work in [Peru](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Peru "Peru") in the 1980s and 1990s, during which he worked as a parish pastor, diocesan official, seminary teacher, and administrator. Elected [prior general](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Superior_general_/(Christianity/) "Superior general (Christianity)") of the Order of Saint Augustine, he was based in Rome from 2001 to 2013, and traveled extensively as part of this work, including to the [order's many provinces](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Order_of_Saint_Augustine#Provinces "Order of Saint Augustine") and [missions](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Order_of_Saint_Augustine#Priories "Order of Saint Augustine") around the world. He then returned to Peru as [Bishop of Chiclayo](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Bishop_of_Chiclayo "Bishop of Chiclayo") from 2015 to 2023. In 2023, Pope Francis appointed him prefect of the [Dicastery for Bishops](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Dicastery_for_Bishops "Dicastery for Bishops") in Rome, and president of the [Pontifical Commission for Latin America](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pontifical_Commission_for_Latin_America "Pontifical Commission for Latin America"). Upon his return to Rome in 2023, Prevost was made a [cardinal](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Cardinal_/(Catholic_Church/) "Cardinal (Catholic Church)") by Pope Francis.

As Cardinal, Prevost emphasized [synodality](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Synodality "Synodality"), missionary dialogue, and engagement with social and technological challenges. He has also addressed issues such as [climate change](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Climate_change "Climate change"), global migration, church governance, and human rights, and expressed alignment with the reforms of the [Second Vatican Council](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Second_Vatican_Council "Second Vatican Council") and the direction set for the Church by Francis.

Prevost's election in the [2025 conclave](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/2025_conclave "2025 conclave") was unexpected by observers; he was a [dark horse](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Dark_horse "Dark horse") candidate, with Vatican insiders believing the prospect of a Pope from the United States to be unrealistic given its status as a [superpower](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Superpower "Superpower").[\[8\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Rocca-2025-11)[\[9\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Horowitz,_Bosman,_Dias,_Graham,_Romero_&_Taj_2025-12) In honor of [Pope Leo XIII](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIII "Pope Leo XIII"), who developed modern [Catholic social teaching](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Catholic_social_teaching "Catholic social teaching") amid the tumult of the [Second Industrial Revolution](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Second_Industrial_Revolution "Second Industrial Revolution"), Prevost chose the [papal name](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Papal_name "Papal name") Leo XIV—both to echo Leo XIII's concern for workers and fairness, and as a response to the challenges of [a new industrial revolution](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Fourth_Industrial_Revolution "Fourth Industrial Revolution") and [artificial intelligence](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Artificial_intelligence "Artificial intelligence").[\[10\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-13)

Early life, family, and education (1955–1973)
---------------------------------------------

### Background and ancestry

Robert Francis Prevost was born on September 14, 1955,[\[11\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Moral_Ant%C3%B3n_2014-14)[\[12\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Vatican_News_2025-15) at [Mercy Hospital](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Insight_Hospital_and_Medical_Center "Insight Hospital and Medical Center") in the [Bronzeville](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Black_Metropolis%E2%80%93Bronzeville_District "Black Metropolis–Bronzeville District") neighborhood of Chicago, Illinois, on the city's [South Side](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/South_Side,_Chicago "South Side, Chicago").[\[13\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-FitzPatrick_2025-16)[\[14\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Bosman_2025-17)[\[15\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-18) He is of [French](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/French_people "French people"),[\[16\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Colas-19) [Italian](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Italians "Italians"),[\[17\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-20)[\[18\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-21) [Spanish](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Spaniards "Spaniards"),[\[19\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Gates_Jr.-2025-22) and [Louisiana Creole](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Louisiana_Creole_people "Louisiana Creole people")[\[20\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-23) descent.[\[19\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Gates_Jr.-2025-22)[\[13\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-FitzPatrick_2025-16)[\[21\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-24)[\[22\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-kim-25) His father, Louis Marius Prevost, was a Chicago native, having grown up in [Hyde Park](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Hyde_Park,_Chicago "Hyde Park, Chicago").[\[23\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-26) Louis's father and mother were immigrants from Italy and France, respectively.[\[24\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-bosman2025-27)[\[3\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Serra_2025-4)[\[25\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Vergun_2025-28) Louis Prevost was a [United States Navy](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/United_States_Navy "United States Navy") veteran of [World War II](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/World_War_II "World War II") who commanded an infantry landing craft in the [Normandy landings](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Normandy_landings "Normandy landings") and later participated in [Operation Dragoon](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Operation_Dragoon "Operation Dragoon") in southern France.[\[25\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Vergun_2025-28) An educator, he later became superintendent of [Brookwood School District 167](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Brookwood_School_District_167 "Brookwood School District 167") in [Glenwood, Illinois](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Glenwood,_Illinois "Glenwood, Illinois").[\[26\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Chicago_Tribune_1997-29)[\[27\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-30) Leo XIV's mother, Mildred Agnes Prevost ([née](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Birth_name#Maiden_and_married_names "Birth name") Martínez),[\[28\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Burack_2025-31)[\[25\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Vergun_2025-28)[\[29\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Rose,_Romine,_&_Rehbein_2025-32) was also born in Chicago, into a mixed-race [Black Creole](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Creoles_of_color "Creoles of color") family from [Louisiana](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Louisiana "Louisiana").[\[29\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Rose,_Romine,_&_Rehbein_2025-32)[\[30\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-33) She was also an educator, and a librarian, including at [Mendel Catholic High School](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Mendel_Catholic_High_School "Mendel Catholic High School").[\[31\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Chicago_Tribune_1990-34)

### Early life and schooling

Known as "Rob" to his family and "Bob" to friends as an adult,[\[13\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-FitzPatrick_2025-16)[\[32\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Griffin_2025-35)[\[33\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-36) Prevost was raised in [Dolton, Illinois](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Dolton,_Illinois "Dolton, Illinois"), a suburb bordering the far South Side; [his childhood home](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV_childhood_home "Pope Leo XIV childhood home") was purchased by the Village of Dolton after he became pope.[\[34\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-doltonhome-37) He grew up in the [parish](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Parish_/(Catholic_Church/) "Parish (Catholic Church)") of [St. Mary of the Assumption](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Saint_Mary_of_the_Assumption_Church_/(Chicago/) "Saint Mary of the Assumption Church (Chicago)") in nearby [Riverdale](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Riverdale,_Chicago "Riverdale, Chicago"). His parents were practicing Catholics who were very involved in the parish: Louis was a [catechist](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Catechist "Catechist"), a teacher of the faith; while Mildred was an active member of the Rosary and [Altar Society](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Altar_Society "Altar Society"), sang in the church [choir](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Choir "Choir"), provided services for the church and went to daily Mass. According to Leo, what influenced him spiritually was his parents' faith, prayer life and [Marian devotions](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Marian_devotion "Marian devotion") ("My parents prayed the [rosary](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Rosary "Rosary") together their whole lives everyday") and their mutual love.[\[35\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-38)[\[28\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Burack_2025-31) His mother would call him and his brothers to go to [Mass](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Mass_in_the_Catholic_Church "Mass in the Catholic Church") before school at 6:30 a.m., and told them that Jesus "is your best friend," and Mass "a way to find that friend."[\[36\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-39) Leo went to the parish [Catholic school](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Catholic_schools_in_the_United_States "Catholic schools in the United States"), sang in the choir, and served as an [altar boy](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Altar_boy "Altar boy").[\[13\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-FitzPatrick_2025-16)[\[37\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-40)[\[d\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-42) Prevost has two older brothers, Louis Martín, and John Joseph.[\[39\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-43) Prevost aspired to the [priesthood](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Priesthood_in_the_Catholic_Church "Priesthood in the Catholic Church") from a young age,[\[32\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Griffin_2025-35) and would play-act the Mass at home with his brothers.[\[40\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Tucker_2025-44)

From 1969 to 1973, Prevost attended [St. Augustine Seminary High School](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/St._Augustine_Seminary_High_School "St. Augustine Seminary High School"), a [minor seminary](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Minor_seminary "Minor seminary") near [Saugatuck, Michigan](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Saugatuck,_Michigan "Saugatuck, Michigan");[\[41\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-45)[\[42\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-46) his brother John recalled how, from the end of [eighth grade](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Eighth_grade "Eighth grade") on, and especially after joining the [Order of Saint Augustine](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Order_of_Saint_Augustine "Order of Saint Augustine"), until their later adulthood when [leave](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Leave_of_absence "Leave of absence") allowed them to reconnect, Prevost was hardly at home or with their family.[\[40\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Tucker_2025-44)

At the Augustinian seminary, he earned a letter of commendation for academic excellence, consistently appeared on the [honor roll](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Honor_roll "Honor roll"), served as [yearbook](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Yearbook "Yearbook") editor-in-chief, and was secretary of the [student council](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Student_council "Student council") and a member of the [National Honor Society](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/National_Honor_Society "National Honor Society").[\[43\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-47)[\[44\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-48) He captained the bowling team and headed the [speech and debate](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Debate "Debate") team, competing in [Congressional Debate](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Congressional_Debate "Congressional Debate").[\[45\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-49)[\[46\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-50) Well-liked and highly intelligent, Prevost had a reputation for helping other students as a tutor.[\[47\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-51) Out of several dozen who entered the school with him, Prevost was one of only 13 students in his class to graduate.[\[9\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Horowitz,_Bosman,_Dias,_Graham,_Romero_&_Taj_2025-12)

University and early priesthood (1973–1998)
-------------------------------------------

### University

In 1973, Prevost was planning to attend [Tolentine College](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Tolentine_College "Tolentine College"), an Augustinian seminary in [Olympia Fields, Illinois](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Olympia_Fields,_Illinois "Olympia Fields, Illinois"), as part of the order's pre-[novitiate](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Novitiate "Novitiate") program, but it closed that same year.[\[9\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Horowitz,_Bosman,_Dias,_Graham,_Romero_&_Taj_2025-12)[\[48\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-FitzPatrick_and_Winfield_2025-52) He promptly enrolled in [Villanova University](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Villanova_University "Villanova University"), an Augustinian college located near [Philadelphia](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Philadelphia "Philadelphia"), where he earned a [Bachelor of Science](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Bachelor_of_Science "Bachelor of Science") (BS) degree in mathematics in 1977.[\[12\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Vatican_News_2025-15)[\[49\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Mervosh_2025-53)[\[50\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-54) At Villanova, he took elective courses in [Hebrew](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Hebrew_language "Hebrew language") and [Latin](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Latin_language "Latin language"), read the writings of [Saint Augustine](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Saint_Augustine "Saint Augustine"), and discussed the work of theologian [Karl Rahner](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Karl_Rahner "Karl Rahner") with other students.[\[9\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Horowitz,_Bosman,_Dias,_Graham,_Romero_&_Taj_2025-12) He lived in the Augustinian [friary](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Monastery "Monastery"), and was remembered as "particularly committed... to missionary work," and being "the most community minded" among the students.[\[51\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-55) Prevost also worked as a cemetery groundskeeper at Saint Denis Catholic Church in [Havertown, Pennsylvania](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Havertown,_Pennsylvania "Havertown, Pennsylvania"), while studying at Villanova.[\[52\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-fox29-56)

### Entry into Augustinians

On September 1, 1977, Prevost entered the [Order of Saint Augustine](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Order_of_Saint_Augustine "Order of Saint Augustine")'s [novitiate](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Novitiate "Novitiate") in the [Province of Our Mother of Good Counsel](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Order_of_St._Augustine_in_the_United_States#Province_of_Our_Mother_of_Good_Counsel_\(Central/Midwestern_Province\) "Order of St. Augustine in the United States"). He resided for one year at [Immaculate Conception Church](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Immaculate_Conception_Church_and_Rectory_/(St._Louis/) "Immaculate Conception Church and Rectory (St. Louis)") in the [Gate District](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Gate_District,_St._Louis "Gate District, St. Louis") neighborhood of [St. Louis, Missouri](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/St._Louis,_Missouri "St. Louis, Missouri").[\[53\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-57)[\[54\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-58)[\[55\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-59)[\[56\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-60) In the summer of 1978, Prevost spent three months in [Clinical Pastoral Education](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Clinical_Pastoral_Education "Clinical Pastoral Education") at [Abbott Northwestern Hospital](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Abbott_Northwestern_Hospital "Abbott Northwestern Hospital") in [Minneapolis](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Minneapolis "Minneapolis").[\[57\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Gomes2025-61)[\[58\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-62)[\[59\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-63) He took his [first vows](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/First_vows "First vows") on September 2, 1978, and his [solemn vows](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Solemn_vow "Solemn vow") on August 29, 1981.[\[11\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Moral_Ant%C3%B3n_2014-14)[\[12\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Vatican_News_2025-15)

He returned to his father's native Hyde Park to obtain a [Master of Divinity](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Master_of_Divinity "Master of Divinity") (MDiv) from [Catholic Theological Union](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Catholic_Theological_Union "Catholic Theological Union") in 1982 and taught physics and math at [St. Rita of Cascia High School](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/St._Rita_of_Cascia_High_School "St. Rita of Cascia High School") in the [Wrightwood](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Wrightwood,_Chicago "Wrightwood, Chicago") neighborhood of Chicago during his studies.[\[13\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-FitzPatrick_2025-16)[\[60\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Rich,_Dias_&_Horowitz_2025-64) As his [spiritual director](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Spiritual_direction "Spiritual direction"), a guide to the Christian life, he chose a [religious sister](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Religious_sister "Religious sister"), Sister Lyn Osiek, [RSCJ](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/RSCJ "RSCJ"), the supervisor of his theological reflection class. She described him as "calm and steady... a person who was at peace with himself."[\[61\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-The_Making_of_an_American_Pope-65)

### Ordination and missionary work in Peru

On September 10, 1981, Prevost was ordained a deacon by [Thomas Gumbleton](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Thomas_Gumbleton "Thomas Gumbleton") at St. [Clare of Montefalco](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Clare_of_Montefalco "Clare of Montefalco") Parish in [Grosse Pointe Park](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Grosse_Pointe_Park "Grosse Pointe Park"), Michigan. That same year, Prevost concluded his studies at Catholic Theological Union.[\[62\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Meloy-66)[\[11\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Moral_Ant%C3%B3n_2014-14) Prevost was [ordained](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Holy_orders_in_the_Catholic_Church "Holy orders in the Catholic Church") a priest in Rome, at the [Chapel of Saint Monica of the Augustinians](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Santa_Monica_degli_Agostiniani "Santa Monica degli Agostiniani") by Archbishop [Jean Jadot](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Jean_Jadot "Jean Jadot") on June 19, 1982.[\[11\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Moral_Ant%C3%B3n_2014-14)[\[12\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Vatican_News_2025-15)[\[63\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Scaramuzzi_2025-67)

Prevost earned a [Licentiate of Canon Law](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Licentiate_of_Canon_Law "Licentiate of Canon Law") (JCL) in 1984, followed by a [Doctor of Canon Law](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Doctor_of_Canon_Law_/(Catholic_Church/) "Doctor of Canon Law (Catholic Church)") (JCD) degree in 1987, both from the [Pontifical University of Saint Thomas Aquinas](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pontifical_University_of_Saint_Thomas_Aquinas "Pontifical University of Saint Thomas Aquinas") in Rome.[\[12\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Vatican_News_2025-15) During this period, he also learned [Italian](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Italian_language "Italian language").[\[9\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Horowitz,_Bosman,_Dias,_Graham,_Romero_&_Taj_2025-12) His doctoral thesis was a [canon law](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Canon_law "Canon law") study of the role of local [priors](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Prior_/(ecclesiastical/) "Prior (ecclesiastical)") in the Order of Saint Augustine.[\[64\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-68)

[![Image 1: Thumb](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f8/Immaculate_Conception_Church_Lafayette_at_Longfellow_St._Louis_MO.jpg/640px-Immaculate_Conception_Church_Lafayette_at_Longfellow_St._Louis_MO.jpg)](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#/media/File:Immaculate_Conception_Church_Lafayette_at_Longfellow_St._Louis_MO.jpg)

Prevost spent his [novitiate](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Novitiate "Novitiate") at Immaculate Conception Church in St. Louis, Missouri.

"Padre Roberto" joined the Augustinian mission in Peru in 1985, serving as [chancellor](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Chancellor_/(ecclesiastical/) "Chancellor (ecclesiastical)") of the [Territorial Prelature of Chulucanas](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Territorial_Prelature_of_Chulucanas "Territorial Prelature of Chulucanas") (1985–1986), as well as an aide to bishop [John McNabb](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Juan_Conway_McNabb "Juan Conway McNabb"). Much of his work in his first year in Peru was focused on disaster relief following severe [El Niño](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/El_Ni%C3%B1o%E2%80%93Southern_Oscillation "El Niño–Southern Oscillation") rainstorms. [\[11\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Moral_Ant%C3%B3n_2014-14)[\[65\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Clarke-2025-69) In 1987, after defending his doctoral thesis, he was vocation director and missions director of the Augustinian [Province of Our Mother of Good Counsel](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Order_of_St._Augustine_in_the_United_States#Province_of_Our_Mother_of_Good_Counsel_\(Central/Midwestern_Province\) "Order of St. Augustine in the United States") in [Olympia Fields, Illinois](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Olympia_Fields,_Illinois "Olympia Fields, Illinois"), and worked with the faculty of the Augustinian Novitiate in [Oconomowoc, Wisconsin](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Oconomowoc,_Wisconsin "Oconomowoc, Wisconsin"), before returning to Peru in 1988.[\[12\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Vatican_News_2025-15)[\[66\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-70) During his time in Peru, Prevost met and appreciated the [Dominican priest](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Order_of_Preachers "Order of Preachers") and theologian [Gustavo Gutierrez](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Gustavo_Gutierrez "Gustavo Gutierrez"), a pioneer of [liberation theology](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Liberation_theology "Liberation theology").[\[63\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Scaramuzzi_2025-67) He also learned and mastered the [Spanish language](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Spanish_language "Spanish language") during this period.[\[9\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Horowitz,_Bosman,_Dias,_Graham,_Romero_&_Taj_2025-12)

Prevost spent a decade heading the Augustinian seminary in [Trujillo](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Trujillo,_Peru "Trujillo, Peru"), teaching [canon law](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Canon_law "Canon law") in the diocesan seminary,[\[12\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Vatican_News_2025-15) serving as prefect of studies, acting as a judge in the regional [ecclesiastical court](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Ecclesiastical_court "Ecclesiastical court"), and working in parish ministry on the city's outskirts, coming into contact with poor farmers and Peruvian [indigenous peoples](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Indigenous_peoples_of_Peru "Indigenous peoples of Peru").[\[67\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-71)[\[65\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Clarke-2025-69)

[![Image 2: Thumb](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d2/Kathedralbasilika_St._Maria%2C_Trujillo%2C_Peru%2C.jpg/640px-Kathedralbasilika_St._Maria%2C_Trujillo%2C_Peru%2C.jpg)](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#/media/File:Kathedralbasilika_St._Maria,_Trujillo,_Peru,.jpg)

Cathedral Basilica of Saint Mary, Trujillo. As a young missionary, Prevost served in various roles in the [Archdiocese of Trujillo](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Archdiocese_of_Trujillo "Archdiocese of Trujillo").

He proved successful in the Augustinians' efforts to recruit Peruvians for the priesthood and leadership positions in the order.[\[68\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-72) He organized support for Venezuelan refugees to Peru despite discrimination against the Venezuelans.[\[69\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-73)

During the _[Fujimorato](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Fujimorato "Fujimorato")_ era, Prevost criticized the actions of then-President [Alberto Fujimori](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Alberto_Fujimori "Alberto Fujimori"), placing special emphasis on the victims of the [Peruvian Army](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Peruvian_Army "Peruvian Army"), especially the [Colina Group](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Colina_Group "Colina Group"), during the [period of terrorism in Peru](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Period_of_terrorism_in_Peru "Period of terrorism in Peru"), as well as on political corruption. In 2017, he criticized President [Pedro Pablo Kuczynski](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pedro_Pablo_Kuczynski "Pedro Pablo Kuczynski")'s decision to [pardon Fujimori](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pardon_of_Alberto_Fujimori "Pardon of Alberto Fujimori"), and called upon Fujimori "to personally apologize for some of the great injustices that were committed".[\[70\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-74) His years in Peru gave him personal knowledge of political violence and inequality; at times, as a missionary, he traveled by horse on difficult roads to reach the isolated communities in the valleys of [Lambayeque](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Department_of_Lambayeque "Department of Lambayeque").[\[71\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-75) He also stood out as a defender of human rights of the population of the [Norte Chico](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Norte_Chico_/(Peruvian_region/) "Norte Chico (Peruvian region)") region against the violence of the [Marxist–Leninist–Maoist](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Marxist%E2%80%93Leninist%E2%80%93Maoist "Marxist–Leninist–Maoist") guerrilla organization [Shining Path](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Shining_Path "Shining Path").[\[72\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-76)[\[73\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-77) However, Trujilio, the area where Prevost served, was not particularly affected by the Shining Path.[\[65\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Clarke-2025-69)

Prior provincial and prior general (1998–2013)
----------------------------------------------

[![Image 3: Thumb](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a0/St._Thomas_Church_and_Convent_--_School_02.jpg/640px-St._Thomas_Church_and_Convent_--_School_02.jpg)](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#/media/File:St._Thomas_Church_and_Convent_--_School_02.jpg)

St. Thomas School in Hyde Park, Chicago

In 1998, Prevost was elected [Prior Provincial](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Prior_Provincial "Prior Provincial") of the Order of St. Augustine's [Province of Our Mother of Good Counsel](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Order_of_St._Augustine_in_the_United_States#Province_of_Our_Mother_of_Good_Counsel_\(Central/Midwestern_Province\) "Order of St. Augustine in the United States") based in Chicago, assuming the role on March 8, 1999.[\[12\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Vatican_News_2025-15) In 2000, he permitted James Ray, an Augustinian priest, to reside at St. John Stone Friary in Chicago under supervision. Ray had been [suspended from public ministry](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Suspension_/(Catholic_canonical_penalty/) "Suspension (Catholic canonical penalty)") since 1991 due to credible accusations that he had [sexually abused minors](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Catholic_Church_sexual_abuse_cases "Catholic Church sexual abuse cases"). Prevost's allowing of the placement of Ray in a friary at the request of the [Archdiocese of Chicago](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Archdiocese_of_Chicago "Archdiocese of Chicago") and close to [St. Thomas School](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/St._Thomas_Church_and_Convent "St. Thomas Church and Convent") was the subject of reporting in 2021, prior to his appointment to the Vatican.[\[74\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-The_Pillar_2021-78) According to the Augustinians, "the location was selected because of the supervision the priest would receive."[\[61\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-The_Making_of_an_American_Pope-65) After American bishops implemented stricter rules in the [Dallas Charter](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Dallas_Charter "Dallas Charter"), Ray was moved to other housing in 2002.[\[74\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-The_Pillar_2021-78)[\[75\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Herguth_2021-79)[\[e\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-80)

Elected [prior general](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Superior_general_/(Christianity/) "Superior general (Christianity)") of the Order of Saint Augustine in 2001, Prevost served two consecutive, six-year terms until 2013.[\[76\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-81) During his tenure as the global head of the Augustinian order, Prevost lived and worked in Rome, but frequently traveled around the world. It was in that capacity that in 2004, he visited Buenos Aires and met Cardinal Jorge Bergoglio, the future [Pope Francis](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Francis "Pope Francis"), for the first time. Their early encounters are reported to have not gone well. Prevost later explained that at the time, he thought he would never become a [bishop](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Bishops_in_the_Catholic_Church "Bishops in the Catholic Church") after Bergoglio was elected Pope in 2013, but has declined to reveal what they initially disagreed upon. However, they were able to reconcile their differences before Prevost left Rome for Chicago in 2013.[\[9\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Horowitz,_Bosman,_Dias,_Graham,_Romero_&_Taj_2025-12) Soon after his election as prior general, Prevost personally oversaw the creation of a web site for the Augustinians.[\[77\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-82)

From 2013 to 2014, Prevost served as director of formation at the Convent of St. Augustine in Chicago, and as first councilor and provincial vicar of the province of Our Mother of Good Counsel.[\[12\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Vatican_News_2025-15)

[![Image 4: Thumb](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9e/Santa_Mar%C3%ADa_Catedral_-_Chiclayo.jpg/640px-Santa_Mar%C3%ADa_Catedral_-_Chiclayo.jpg)](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#/media/File:Santa_Mar%C3%ADa_Catedral_-_Chiclayo.jpg)

[St. Mary's Cathedral](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/St._Mary's_Cathedral,_Chiclayo "St. Mary's Cathedral, Chiclayo") in [Chiclayo](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Chiclayo "Chiclayo"), Peru, where Prevost was diocesan bishop from 2015 to 2023

On November 3, 2014, Pope Francis appointed Prevost as the [apostolic administrator](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Apostolic_administrator "Apostolic administrator") of the [Diocese of Chiclayo](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Diocese_of_Chiclayo "Diocese of Chiclayo") in northern Peru and the [titular bishop](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Titular_bishop "Titular bishop") of [Sufar](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Sufar "Sufar").[\[78\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-83) He was consecrated on December 12, 2014, at [St. Mary Cathedral](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/St._Mary's_Cathedral_in_Chiclayo "St. Mary's Cathedral in Chiclayo") by Archbishop [James Green](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/James_Green_/(bishop/) "James Green (bishop)"), [Apostolic Nuncio to Peru](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Apostolic_Nuncio_to_Peru "Apostolic Nuncio to Peru").[\[79\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-84)[\[80\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-85) On September 26, 2015, he was named Bishop of Chiclayo.[\[81\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-86)[\[82\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-87) As required by a 1980 agreement between the Holy See and [Peru](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Peru "Peru"),[\[83\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-88) Prevost became a [naturalized Peruvian citizen](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Naturalized_Peruvian_citizen "Naturalized Peruvian citizen") before becoming bishop.[\[60\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Rich,_Dias_&_Horowitz_2025-64) At the time of his appointment, Chiclayo was described as a conservative diocese, having been staffed by [Opus Dei](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Opus_Dei "Opus Dei") priests for many decades.[\[65\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Clarke-2025-69)

Prevost developed a close bond with the diocese of Chiclayo, directing a special message to them in his first message as Pope, calling them "my beloved diocese", "faithful people" and "faithful church".[\[84\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Olmo-2025-89)[\[85\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-90) He was seen as being "very faithful to the [Church's social doctrine](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Catholic_social_teaching "Catholic social teaching")" and organized relief efforts during calamities. He also supported projects in favor of Venezuelan refugees and encouraged vocations in youth groups, giving strong support to the seminary.[\[86\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Beltr%C3%A1n-91) He helped victims of trafficking and sex workers learn new skills and trades, and invited them to spiritual retreats, while ensuring that volunteer workers have adequate training. He is remembered for his capacity to listen and have discussions with different groups before taking action, and working with institutions when facing controversial issues.[\[87\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Rueda-92) He established a diocesan Commission on Integral Ecology and appointed a woman to lead it.[\[84\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Olmo-2025-89) According to interviews done by _[The Pillar](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/The_Pillar "The Pillar")_, people in the diocese described their bishop as having a "balanced" personality, a "calming presence", showing "great charity and great clarity" in doctrinal matters, and a competent administrator and bridge-builder open to dialogue and never hurtful, with "[apostolic zeal](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Evangelism "Evangelism")"[\[86\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Beltr%C3%A1n-91)

Prevost as Bishop of Chiclayo in 2018, commenting on extreme poverty in the region (in Spanish)

On July 13, 2019, Prevost was appointed a member of the [Congregation for the Clergy](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Congregation_for_the_Clergy "Congregation for the Clergy"),[\[88\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-93) and on April 15, 2020, he became apostolic administrator of [Callao](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Roman_Catholic_Diocese_of_Callao "Roman Catholic Diocese of Callao").[\[89\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-94)[\[f\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-95) On November 21, 2020, he joined the [Congregation for Bishops](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Congregation_for_Bishops "Congregation for Bishops").[\[90\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-96) Within the [Episcopal Conference of Peru](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Episcopal_Conference_of_Peru "Episcopal Conference of Peru"), he served on the permanent council (2018–2020) and was elected president of its Commission for Education and Culture in 2019, also contributing to [Caritas](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Caritas_Internationalis "Caritas Internationalis") Peru.[\[91\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Wells,_Olmo_&_Sullivan_2025-97)[\[92\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-98) His presence in the permanent council of the episcopal conference was seen by Cardinal [Joseph Tobin](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Joseph_Tobin "Joseph Tobin") as "extraordinary for someone who was not born in Peru. Clearly, he has a broad degree of acceptance in the divided group."[\[93\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-99) Prevost had a private audience with Pope Francis on March 1, 2021,[\[94\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-100) sparking speculation about a new role in Chicago or Rome.[\[95\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-101)

Prevost has been accused of covering up [sexual abuse](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Catholic_Church_sexual_abuse_cases "Catholic Church sexual abuse cases") during his time in Chiclayo.[\[96\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Will_County_Gazette_2025-102)[\[97\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-The_Jerusalem_Post_2025-103) In 2022, alleged victims of abuse in 2007 by priests Ricardo Yesquén Paiva and Eleuterio Vásquez Gonzáles said the Diocese of Chiclayo failed to investigate their cases.[\[98\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-104) The [Diocese of Chiclayo](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Roman_Catholic_Diocese_of_Chiclayo "Roman Catholic Diocese of Chiclayo") stated that Prevost followed proper procedures, met with Ana María Quispe and her sisters in April 2022 to personally attend the victims, encouraged them to initiate a civil action, and initiated a canonical investigation, the results of which he sent to the [Dicastery for the Doctrine of the Faith](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Dicastery_for_the_Doctrine_of_the_Faith "Dicastery for the Doctrine of the Faith").[\[99\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-105)[\[100\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-106) The sisters stated in 2024 that no full penal canonical investigation occurred, and an investigation by [América Televisión](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Am%C3%A9rica_Televisi%C3%B3n "América Televisión") concluded that the church's investigation was not thorough.[\[101\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-107)[\[102\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-108)

In response the diocese of Chiclayo stated the allegations of the TV program were false, calling on it to correct its inaccuracies. The diocese said that the accused priest "never admitted" to the accusations, that Prevost prohibited him from exercising the priestly ministry and the priest transferred residence to his family's home. Prevost submitted the dossier to the Vatican, which gave a "pro nunc" decision or temporary dismissal. The diocese later reopened the case and sent it to the Vatican anew, and thus it remains "open up to now."[\[103\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-109)

Speaking to the Peruvian newspaper _[La República](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/La_Rep%C3%BAblica_/(Peru/) "La República (Peru)")_ while Bishop of Chiclayo, Prevost said: "If you are a victim of sexual abuse by a priest, report it. We reject cover-ups and secrecy; that causes a lot of harm. We have to help people who have suffered due to wrongdoing."[\[104\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-110)[\[105\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-AFP_2025-111)[\[g\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-112) Journalist Pedro Salinas ([es](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pedro_Salinas_/(periodista/) "es:Pedro Salinas (periodista)")), who investigated and exposed crimes committed by members of the now-defunct [Sodalitium Christianae Vitae](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Sodalitium_Christianae_Vitae "Sodalitium Christianae Vitae")—including sexual, physical, and psychological abuse—has argued that Prevost always expressed his support for the victims and was one of the most reliable clerical authorities in Peru, leading Pope Francis to select him as prefect of bishops. Salinas has written that some of the Peruvian clerics linked to the Sodalitium sought to attack and defame Prevost in retaliation for his role in the Sodalitium's dissolution by Pope Francis due to its sexual abuse scandals, as well as Prevost being near to [Francis's political theology](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Theology_of_Pope_Francis "Theology of Pope Francis").[\[106\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-113)[\[107\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-114)

Dicastery for Bishops and cardinalate (2023–2025)
-------------------------------------------------

[![Image 5: Thumb](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/85/Procesija_s_pok._papom_Franjom_%287%29.jpg/250px-Procesija_s_pok._papom_Franjom_%287%29.jpg)](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#/media/File:Procesija_s_pok._papom_Franjom_\(7\).jpg)

Cardinal Prevost (first from right) during the procession with the body of Pope Francis, April 23, 2025

[![Image 6: Thumb](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/00/Cardinal_Robert_F._Prevost_at_the_Consistory_on_30_September_2023_%283x4_cropped%29.jpg/250px-Cardinal_Robert_F._Prevost_at_the_Consistory_on_30_September_2023_%283x4_cropped%29.jpg)](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#/media/File:Cardinal_Robert_F._Prevost_at_the_Consistory_on_30_September_2023_\(3x4_cropped\).jpg)

Prevost during the Consistory in 2023

By the 2020s, Pope Francis had become close to Prevost and advanced his career.[\[9\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Horowitz,_Bosman,_Dias,_Graham,_Romero_&_Taj_2025-12)[\[108\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Bubola-115) On January 30, 2023, Francis appointed Prevost prefect of the [Dicastery for Bishops](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Dicastery_for_Bishops "Dicastery for Bishops") with the title Archbishop-Bishop emeritus of Chiclayo.[\[109\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-116)[\[110\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-117) Prevost expressed a preference to stay in Peru, but accepted the appointment.[\[108\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Bubola-115) He continued to be active in the Latin American and Caribbean Episcopal Council and participated in the council's meetings in [Aguadilla, Puerto Rico](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Aguadilla,_Puerto_Rico "Aguadilla, Puerto Rico"), in May 2023.[\[111\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-118)

On September 30, 2023, Francis created Prevost a cardinal with the rank of Cardinal-Deacon and assigned the deaconry of [Santa Monica degli Agostiniani](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Santa_Monica_degli_Agostiniani "Santa Monica degli Agostiniani").[\[112\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-119) As prefect, he played a critical role in [evaluating and recommending episcopal candidates](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Appointment_of_Catholic_bishops "Appointment of Catholic bishops") worldwide, increasing his visibility within the church.[\[113\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-120) These roles elevated his prominence as a papal candidate leading into the conclave.[\[114\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-NCR_2025-121)[\[115\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-122)[\[116\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-123) In October 2023, Francis appointed him as a member of seven additional [dicasteries](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Dicasteries "Dicasteries"),[\[12\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Vatican_News_2025-15)[\[h\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-124) and also named him to the [Pontifical Commission for the Vatican City State](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pontifical_Commission_for_the_Vatican_City_State "Pontifical Commission for the Vatican City State").[\[12\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Vatican_News_2025-15)

On February 6, 2025, Francis promoted Prevost to cardinal-bishop, assigning him as [titular bishop](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Titular_bishop "Titular bishop") of the [Suburbicarian Diocese of Albano](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Suburbicarian_Diocese_of_Albano "Suburbicarian Diocese of Albano").[\[117\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-125)[\[118\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-126)[\[i\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-128) On February 11, he was appointed to the dignity and rank of [Bailiff](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Bailiff "Bailiff") Grand Cross of Honour and Devotion of the [Order of Malta](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Sovereign_Military_Order_of_Malta "Sovereign Military Order of Malta") by [Grand Master](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Grand_Master_of_the_Order_of_St._John_of_Jerusalem "Grand Master of the Order of St. John of Jerusalem") Fra' [John Dunlap](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/John_T._Dunlap "John T. Dunlap").[\[120\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-129)

Written works before the papacy and theology of leadership
----------------------------------------------------------

Given his focus on mission, the writings of Prevost before his election were few.[\[121\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-130)[\[122\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-131) When he was global head of the Augustinians, the _Rule and Constitutions of the Order of Saint Augustine_ was "issued by Authority of the Prior General, Robert F. Prevost" in 2002.[\[123\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-132)

Aside from four journal articles published mostly in Augustininan journals, his main work of scholarship is his doctoral dissertation, _The office and authority of the local Prior in the Order of Saint Augustine_, published by the Pontifical University of Saint Thomas Aquinas in 1987. The work has been noted for its legal precision, Augustinian roots, [postconciliar engagement](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Second_Vatican_Council "Second Vatican Council") and historical depth.[\[124\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Towell-2025-1-133) Much of the commentary see this work as a window to his "vision of the church" and "theology of leadership."[\[125\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Towell-2025-2-134)[\[126\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-U-Sydney-135)[\[127\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-136)

In his thesis, Prevost sees that authority is received from above, and therefore "the substance of the office of the superior is to obey; to obey the will of God and to put great effort into trying to know it, to formulate it and to specify it for his subjects."[\[124\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Towell-2025-1-133) Leadership is based on [Jesus Christ's threefold offices of teaching, sanctifying and governing](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Threefold_office "Threefold office"), who sanctifies by prayer and builds community by being centered on the Mass, having "the care of the Brothers, 'especially in spiritual matters.'" The prior must help make the sacraments regular and reverent, protecting "each brother's freedom of conscience while promoting 'frequent' confession."[\[125\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Towell-2025-2-134)

Based on St. Augustine's concept, Prevost sees authority as a service.[\[128\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-137) He says that service means "listening to what the Spirit is saying in His people so that His projects can be carried out freely and willingly. The Prior then is called to listen, so that together they can discern and implement what the Spirit inspires."[\[126\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-U-Sydney-135)

### Election

[![Image 7: Thumb](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a2/Pope_Leo_XIV_on_the_loggia.jpg/640px-Pope_Leo_XIV_on_the_loggia.jpg)](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#/media/File:Pope_Leo_XIV_on_the_loggia.jpg)

Pope Leo XIV waving from the loggia of St. Peter's Basilica in his first public appearance

In pre-conclave speculation, Prevost was considered a [dark horse](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Dark_horse "Dark horse") compared to more prominent _[papabili](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Papabili "Papabili")_,[\[129\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Maddox_&_Gooch_2025-138)[\[130\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-139) although he was noted to be an ally of Pope Francis and a possible compromise candidate.[\[129\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Maddox_&_Gooch_2025-138)[\[131\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-140) His American nationality had been regarded as a potential stumbling block to his candidacy, reflecting unease about enhancing the United States's geopolitical power.[\[8\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Rocca-2025-11)[\[132\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-141) Prevost was well aware of this, explaining to a friend by text message: "I'm an American, I can't be elected".[\[9\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Horowitz,_Bosman,_Dias,_Graham,_Romero_&_Taj_2025-12) Supporters argued that he represented a "dignified [middle of the road](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Via_media "Via media")".[\[133\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Rich_2025-142)

Prevost was elected Pope on May 8, 2025, the second day of the [conclave](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Papal_conclave "Papal conclave"), on the fourth ballot. White smoke appeared from the [Sistine Chapel](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Sistine_Chapel "Sistine Chapel") at 18:07 [CEST](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Central_European_Summer_Time "Central European Summer Time") ([UTC+2](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/UTC+2 "UTC+2")), signifying to the public that a Pope had been chosen.[\[134\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-143) After accepting his election and adopting his [papal name](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Papal_name "Papal name"), Leo embraced his fellow cardinals upon exiting the Sistine Chapel. Cardinal [Dominique Mamberti](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Dominique_Mamberti "Dominique Mamberti"), the [cardinal protodeacon](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Cardinal_protodeacon "Cardinal protodeacon"), made the traditional [Latin](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Latin "Latin") proclamation, __[Habemus papam](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Habemus_papam "Habemus papam")__, announcing Pope Leo XIV to the public for the first time from the central [loggia](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Loggia "Loggia") of [St. Peter's Basilica](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/St._Peter's_Basilica "St. Peter's Basilica").[\[135\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-144)[\[136\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Galeazzi_2025-145) According to [Italian law enforcement](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Law_enforcement_in_Italy "Law enforcement in Italy"), by the time of the _[habemus papam](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Habemus_papam "Habemus papam")_ announcement, there were up to 150,000 in the square.[\[137\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-146)

Leo appeared wearing the traditional [papal stole](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Papal_regalia_and_insignia "Papal regalia and insignia") and [mozzetta](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Mozzetta "Mozzetta"),[\[138\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-147) vestments [Pope Francis](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Francis "Pope Francis") did not wear upon his greeting of the world following his election.[\[139\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-148)[\[140\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Palma_2025-149) His [pectoral cross](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pectoral_cross "Pectoral cross") was one he wore during the conclave, a gift from the Postulator General of the Augustinian Order when he became a cardinal, containing relics from Saint Augustine and his mother [Saint Monica](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Saint_Monica "Saint Monica"), among others.[\[141\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-150) He then delivered his first address to Rome and the world in Italian, advocating for peace and dialogue, expressing gratitude for the legacy of Pope Francis and quoting Saint Augustine; he also greeted his former diocese of Chiclayo, Peru, in Spanish. After the speech, he imparted his first _[Urbi et Orbi](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Urbi_et_Orbi "Urbi et Orbi")_ blessing in Latin.[\[142\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-151)[\[143\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-152)[\[144\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-153)

Leo XIV is the first Pope from the [Order of Saint Augustine](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Order_of_Saint_Augustine "Order of Saint Augustine") and the second Pope from [the Americas](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/The_Americas "The Americas") (after Pope Francis), and is counted as the 267th pope.[\[145\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-154)[\[12\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Vatican_News_2025-15)[\[146\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Kirby_&_Wells_2025-155)[\[j\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-156) He is a [dual citizen](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Dual_citizenship "Dual citizenship") of [Peru](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Peru "Peru") and the [United States](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/United_States "United States").[\[147\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Burga_2025-157)[\[148\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-158)[\[149\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-159) He is the first American pope,[\[150\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-160) in [the sense of being](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/American_/(word/) "American (word)") the first born in the United States.[\[151\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-161)[\[152\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-162)[\[153\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-163) He is the second to be a native English speaker, after the English-born [Adrian IV](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Adrian_IV "Adrian IV") (r. 1154–1159), who would have spoken [Middle English](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Middle_English "Middle English").[\[154\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-164) Leo is also the first Pope born after [World War II](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/World_War_II "World War II") and during the [Cold War](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Cold_War "Cold War"), and thus the first to be born in the [Baby Boomer](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Baby_Boomer "Baby Boomer") generation.[\[155\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-165)[\[156\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-166) While Leo is the first Pope from the Order of Saint Augustine,[\[157\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-167)[\[158\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-168) six previous popes belonged to other orders which follow the [Augustinian Rule](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Rule_of_Saint_Augustine "Rule of Saint Augustine"), the last one prior to Leo being [Pope Eugene IV](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Eugene_IV "Pope Eugene IV") (1431–1447).[\[159\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-169)

### Inauguration

[![Image 8: Thumb](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/ef/Pope_Leo_XIV_in_the_popemobile_at_his_inauguration.jpg/640px-Pope_Leo_XIV_in_the_popemobile_at_his_inauguration.jpg)](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#/media/File:Pope_Leo_XIV_in_the_popemobile_at_his_inauguration.jpg)

Pope Leo XIV's first [popemobile](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Popemobile "Popemobile") ride during his inauguration

On May 9, the day after his election, Leo celebrated his first [Mass](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Mass_in_the_Catholic_Church "Mass in the Catholic Church") as Pope in the Sistine Chapel before the assembled [College of Cardinals](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/College_of_Cardinals "College of Cardinals"). During the Mass, he preached against the lack of faith in the world, and spoke of a church that would act as a "beacon that illuminates the dark nights of this world".[\[160\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-170) Media reported that Leo would take up permanent residence in the [papal apartments](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Papal_apartments "Papal apartments") in the [Apostolic Palace](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Apostolic_Palace "Apostolic Palace") rather than in the [Domus Sanctae Marthae](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Domus_Sanctae_Marthae "Domus Sanctae Marthae") where Francis lived.[\[161\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-171)[\[162\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-172)[\[163\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-173)

Leo's [inauguration Mass](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Papal_inauguration_of_Pope_Leo_XIV "Papal inauguration of Pope Leo XIV") was held on May 18 in [St. Peter's Square](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/St._Peter's_Square "St. Peter's Square").[\[164\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-174)[\[165\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Vatican-Inauguration-2025-175)[\[166\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-Petrine-176) During the Mass, he received the [pallium](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pallium "Pallium") and his [Ring of the Fisherman](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Ring_of_the_Fisherman "Ring of the Fisherman") before 12 representatives of the people of God, including cardinals and bishops, who vowed obedience to the new pope.[\[167\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-177) On May 25, he was formally installed as [Bishop of Rome](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Bishop_of_Rome "Bishop of Rome") in a ceremony at the [Archbasilica of Saint John Lateran](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Archbasilica_of_Saint_John_Lateran "Archbasilica of Saint John Lateran").[\[168\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-178)

### Post-election reactions and impact

In [Chiclayo](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Chiclayo "Chiclayo"), thousands crowded the city square for a Mass of Thanksgiving following Leo's election. Similar Masses were celebrated all over Peru.[\[169\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-179) In the US, over 30,000 Americans gathered at Chicago's [Rate Field](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Rate_Field "Rate Field") for a youth-focused celebration with a video message of Leo XIV who urged Catholics to be "beacons of hope".[\[170\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-180)

Political leaders sent their congratulations. President [Donald Trump](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Donald_Trump "Donald Trump") stated that it is "a Great Honor for our Country", while Vice President [JD Vance](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/JD_Vance "JD Vance"), a Catholic, talked about Catholics and other Christians praying "for his successful work leading the Church". The European Council President [António Costa](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Ant%C3%B3nio_Costa "António Costa") said it was "a moment of hope".[\[171\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-181)

O'Malley endorsed the selection, describing Verny as "a collaborative leader committed to advancing the global adoption of protection and safeguarding, to as best possible assure the safety of those in the care of the Church throughout the world."[\[173\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-McElwee_PCPM_2025-183) On July 6, Leo revived the papal practice of taking summer residence at the [Castel Gandolfo](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Palace_of_Castel_Gandolfo "Palace of Castel Gandolfo"), which Francis had discontinued.[\[174\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Pope_Leo_XIV#cite_note-184)
